additionalProperties.value: Veneer to IRAM 220073b0: clears the output-queue reset guard and rebuilds the queue through 220072cc. The common cursor reset at 220071b0 also handles underrun recovery. Calling convention belongs to the IRAM target and remains untyped here.

Veneer to 22001ed0 returning the frame clock in r0. The native game loop samples it around frame callbacks and divides the elapsed value by 1000 for millisecond pacing, supporting microsecond units. Counter wrap and underlying clock source remain unverified.
Saves r0-r12,lr (56 bytes), passes sp to 0x0804b398, then restores the frame and returns with MOVS pc,lr. Frame[0]=operation, frame[1]=argument, frame[13]=return PC.

Programs AES MMIO at 38c00000. Returns 0x28 for zero bytes, 9 for nonmultiple-of-16 length or unsupported key selector. Selector 0 loads a supplied 16-byte key; selectors 1/2 use hardware selection. Loads supplied 16-byte IV in register byte order, or zero IV when null, programs input/output and starts hardware. Direction is reduced to zero/nonzero. Returns 0 after submission; this body contains no completion poll.

Lazily allocates/initializes an 8-byte mutex, locks it, calls Crypto_AESProcessBufferHardware with all seven arguments, unlocks and returns hardware status. Can allocate and block; unsuitable for an allocation-free PCM callback without a broader execution-context design.

Copies a media-list entry into the destination list. The third argument is an insertion cursor, validated by MediaList_ValidateInsertionCursor and passed to MediaList_LinkEntryAfterCursor. Normal OTG append callers pass NULL. Handles nested entries, duplicate suppression, allocation, and notifications.
Null returns -50. Otherwise destroys the embedded path value at +4, frees the surrounding 16-byte object, and returns 0. Used in context cleanup and failed storage initialization.
Calls registry initializer 082d13d0 once, guarded by a global byte, then returns 0. Called before looking up/claiming storage context records. No locking is visible in this wrapper.

Opens the path descriptor for writing, stages bytes in temporary storage, writes the requested length and updates file length after a full write. Releases temporary/file resources on exit. Returns zero on success, -50 for invalid arguments, -43 on open failure, or a write failure code; a null buffer is allowed only for zero bytes.
Returns the entry at a zero-based ordered index, or NULL for an invalid list/index or unavailable cache. Normalizes order/reversal and lazily builds the order cache.
Branch thunk to HoldSwitch_GetLogicalState at 0807bf74. Returns 1 for locked and 0 for unlocked.

Maps a linked entry to its zero-based ordered index, normalizing order/reversal. Lazily builds the forward index and inverse map at list+0x470+4*mode. Returns -1 for invalid input or an unavailable map.

Prepares the random hardware, seeds it once at MMIO 0x3c100008 using RTC bytes, a platform value, timer register and incoming r4, then discards 19 warm-up words. Reads one result and restores the prior gate state. Later calls skip seeding. Incoming r4 contributes to the seed in the actual instructions; entropy quality is not established.
Returns the current global entry-ID counter, then increments it for the next allocation.
Returns bit 0 of the imported SysInfo flags at offset 0x94.
Production SVC callback: MOV r0, #0; BX lr. The vector wrapper restores the caller registers.
Returns the heap base from literal 0804b44c (stock 08b32b58) and size = SysInfo RAM base + RAM size - heap base. Caller 0806be98 passes the region to the main memory-pool initializer.
For zero delay_value, dispatches to the scheduler yield veneer. Otherwise forwards (0, delay_value) to the delay veneer. Delay units are not established by this wrapper.
Forwards context to FairPlay_ReleaseDecryptionContext and returns its status. The two status multipliers multiply to 1 modulo 2^32. This adapter is used at the game/media integration boundary.
Calls deleting destructor on nonzero/non-minus-one native file handle; returns zero.
Invokes the deleting destructor for handles other than NULL and -1. Returns zero.
r0={uint16 volume,char path[258]}, r1=data fourcc (unused here), r2=mode 1 read or 2/3 write, r3=handle output. Return r0 zero on success.

Opens the volume-prefixed path descriptor: uint16 volume followed by path bytes. Mode 1 reads; 2/3 write. Writes the allocated handle on success and returns zero; invalid arguments return -50. file_type is unused. Frees failed opens and maps native errors.
r0 native file handle, r1 buffer, r2 bytes, r3 flags, stack argument uint32 bytes-read output. Zero success; flags 0 uses normal read.

Reads from a legacy handle into buffer and reports the byte count. Flags bit 1 selects the alternate read path. Returns zero on success; maps native file errors to legacy status values. Rejects handle -1 or NULL buffer with -50.
r0 native file handle, r1 buffer, r2 bytes, r3 flags, stack argument uint32 bytes-written output. Zero success; flag 1 calls native flush.

Writes buffer to a legacy handle and reports the byte count. Flags bit 0 flushes after a successful write. Returns zero on success and maps native file errors; rejects handle -1 or NULL buffer with -50.
Branch thunk to CryptoRandom_NextWord at 08049a14; returns a hardware random word using the backend initialization and gate-state handling.

Allocates a 16-byte descriptor and a 0x2000-byte aligned workspace split into two 0x1000-byte pages. Stores wrapper, page pointers and page size, then publishes descriptor. Returns -108 if descriptor allocation fails, otherwise zero. Nested aligned allocation is assumed successful.
Branch thunk to System_QueueTone at 0807c67c. Allocates and posts the two tone arguments to queue 2 as event 5.
Branch thunk to OnTheGo_AddSelection at 0807c6bc. Index -1 appends the source list; returns zero on success or -41 when unavailable/full.
Invalidates and rebuilds order mode 2, then assigns consecutive song ranks 1..count in its existing order. Assumes rebuilding succeeds; does not choose a new random order.

Reads one full block from storage interface 0, then copies the requested in-block slice to output. Validates offset and slice bounds, resolves record to a block address, wipes/releases the temporary block and balances resource 0x33. Returns zero on success or -1. Used for sidr digest storage; underlying medium is not established here.

Reads one full block from storage interface 0, compares the requested slice, and rewrites the block only when bytes differ. Validates bounds, wipes/releases temporary storage and balances resource 0x33. Returns zero on success or -1. This is a persistent storage mutation, not a RAM-only digest update.

Lazily allocates a mutex and serializes SHA-1 backend access. Flag bit 0 at +0x50 selects fresh initialization versus state restore; feeds input then bit 1 selects final digest versus intermediate-state save to +0x4c. Unlocks and returns zero. Helper results are not propagated.

Converts the EQ menu index with EQ_MenuIndexToSettingsId, updates uint16 settings+0xb64 if changed, persists/notifies through 08053794, and calls the player EQ method at vtable+0xa0 with the low byte. Returns zero. The default decompiler signature includes scratch-register inputs; the true ABI needs caller confirmation.
Walks 21 task descriptors of 20 bytes twice: first creates every configured task, then starts them. The table includes GraphicsManager, so UI tasks may run before startup returns.

Startup loader for Photo Database, ArtworkDB and iTunesDB, followed by media/playlist indices and related library services. Obtains an 8-byte device identity and creates or reuses the FairPlay storage handle rooted at iPod_Control/iTunes/, then processes sync response state. Also loads preferences and voice-memo/library state. Performs file I/O, allocations and progress notifications; returned status covers the broader startup path, not only DRM initialization.

Requires nonnull base/name/output and encoded strlen divisible by four. Decodes each group as [in2^ca,in0^a6,in3^01,in1^4a], appends it to base in a newly allocated 16-byte path object, and classifies its storage mode at +0xc. On success writes output_path and returns 0; invalid inputs/allocation path return an error. Wipes/frees the temporary decoded name. Used for IC-Info.sidb/sidd/sidv/sidr/sidl and IC-Info.rbSyncResp.

Resolves the opaque storage handle through 083424b4. Record +0xc controls release: zero skips destruction, one destroys owned parsed objects +0x60..0x70, all six path objects +0xa0..0xb4 and allocated base path +8, clearing those pointers and identity state. Larger counts take the reference-decrement path. Returns a 32-bit status; the decompiler second return word is incidental register state.

Returns the decoded format word stored at context +8, or zero for a null context. The protected sample-entry parser uses this as the replacement sample format after successful context creation; the stored word is encoded, not a plain FourCC.

Obfuscated front end used by media and game loading. Rejects null context with 0xffff5bd9 and a context+0x10 encoded-flag condition with 0xffff5bc6. Builds request {context,input,output,reserved,bytes,0,0} for 0831bf88 and returns its status unchanged. Constant products on byte count and final status reduce to identity modulo 2^32. Input/output may alias as the game caller does.

Optionally reads wall-clock day/seconds fields and writes sign-extended 32-bit Unix seconds: (day-2440588)*86400 + seconds. A second optional output uses cached day/seconds as day*86400 + seconds. Returns zero or mapped clock-read error. Arithmetic is 32-bit before sign extension; the second output's epoch is not established here.

Creates/reuses a storage registry record for base_path and returns its opaque numeric handle through output_handle. Identity inputs are length-prefixed byte strings; library caller supplies 8 device bytes, game caller 6 bytes. Initializes six IC-Info path objects and refreshes storage with selector 0x10. Record +8 owns the base path, +0xc tracks references, +0x60..0x70 hold parsed objects, and +0xa0..0xb4 hold paths. Returns status and cleans partial path allocations on failure. Internal identity/flag validation remains obfuscated.

Validates all three pointers (-50 on null), checks embedded path existence (-43 if absent), loads file contents, allocates/copies a caller-owned buffer and returns pointer/size with status 0. Allocation failure returns -108. Marks path-object byte 0 on success and destroys temporary file wrappers. Caller releases output_data through 08023ef0.

Resolves storage_handle and calls 082de3c8 with .sinf bytes, mode, options and parsed registry objects to produce a per-stream decryption context. Media parser 0809d6c4 passes a complete sinf atom, options 0/0 and mode 1, then stores successful context in a mode-3 crypto slot. If record +0x6c has dirty byte +0x21, serializes/persists it through sidr path +0xac; persistence failure releases the newly created context. Frees serialized temporary data and returns status. Option semantics are unresolved; may allocate and write storage.
Sends the low byte of r0 using SYS_WRITEC (3), SVC 0x123456.
Writes the low byte of character using semihosting SYS_WRITEC (3), SVC 0x123456. Requires a semihosting handler.
Gets the platform heap region, stores its base/size at manager offsets +0xd8/+0xdc, then calls 080cc0bc to initialize the memory pool.
Returns arithmetic_shift_right_16(low32(sample*gain_q15)<<1). Used for speed overlap fades. Computes in 32 bits without saturation, so valid fixed-point ranges are a caller requirement.

Reads Manifest.plist with a null signature path, selects an executable by platform ID/version, requires a nonempty Name, and copies Version, UserDataPath, localized names, and optional LaunchingArtwork.
Enables SHA engine resource, clears MMIO 0x38000004/10 and the 64-bit byte counter, then sets engine_control=2 for initial processing. Does not process input or acquire the global SHA mutex itself.

Appends SHA-1 0x80/zero padding and big-endian 64-bit bit length to the partial block, submits one or two blocks, copies 20 digest bytes from hardware and releases engine resource. Mutates partial block and control; caller holds the shared SHA mutex.
Maps menu indices 0..22 through the uint32 table at 083e2568 to stored EQ IDs [0,100..121]. r0=index, r1=uint32 output pointer; zero success, -50 for NULL. No stock input bounds check.

Maps menu index through the 23-word table at 083e2568 to stored EQ ID (0,100..121). Writes settings_id and returns 0; null output returns -50. Caller must keep index in 0..22 because this body has no bounds check.
Returns logical Hold state: 1 locked, 0 unlocked. Converts raw 0/1 from 082da704 to 1 - raw; other values return 0.
Allocates a 24-byte message, stores tone parameters at +0x10/+0x14, and posts event 5 to task/queue 2 through 0802d058. Alarm and alert callers use pairs including (540,200) and (676,200).

Appends one selection, or the whole source list for index -1, to On-The-Go. Enforces the 1000-entry limit, mirrors additions into the active OTG playback list, and marks preferences dirty. Returns zero on success or -41 when unavailable/full.

Adds bytes to the 64-bit count, submits aligned full blocks to SHA DMA at MMIO 0x38000080/84/8c, splitting runs above 0xffc0 bytes. Polls engine busy bit after submissions, copies the remaining 0..63 bytes into partial_block, and switches control to continuation value 10. Blocking hardware path; synchronization is external.
Allocates an entry from list+0x3c, sets its owner and a new global entry ID, and clears the first flags byte at +0x1c. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Temporarily replaces the last byte with NUL, emits SYS_WRITE0, then emits and restores that byte. Requires writable input.
Emits a nonempty writable span through semihosting. Temporarily replaces the final byte with NUL for SYS_WRITE0, writes that saved byte with SYS_WRITEC, then restores it. length must be positive.

Formats and draws text into the caller's pixel buffer using a native 2D context: 320x240 bounds, 0x280-byte row stride, 16-bit depth. Called after the game frame callback with runtime+0x38 as the buffer.
Translates executable addresses 0x18000000..0x180fffff through descriptor 08a10718. Other addresses pass through unchanged.

Copies five SHA state MMIO words from 0x38000020 as 20 little-endian bytes to output, then disables/releases engine resource (1,0). The state argument is unused by this leaf. Caller arranges completion and synchronization.

Nonreturning media reader worker. Obtains packets from provider vtable +0x1c, processes protected bytes through crypto slot 1 into the shared output buffer, and uses IRAM fallback 220084dc when slot mode is zero. Releases each provider packet through +0x20, submits output to consumer +0x40, and posts timing/state metadata and end-of-stream messages. Waits on global synchronization between runs; this is upstream of PCM effects, not an in-place PCM callback.

HoldSwitch descriptor callback (089ca38c). ABI int(unused, void *out, uint32_t *inout_size, unused). Requires capacity >=1, calls 0807bf74, copies one byte, sets size=1, and returns 0. Insufficient capacity returns -48.

Inserts a node using cursor {parent, predecessor}. NULL appends under the list root; predecessor -1 selects the tail, 0 inserts at the head, and other values insert after that node. Node fields: +4 parent, +8 next, +0xc previous. Updates root/ancestor counts and invalidates order caches.
Maps kinds 0/4 to games_RO, 1 to gamedata_RW, 2 to gamestats_WO, and 3 to gamedata_ShareRW. Unknown kinds return the empty suffix string.

Enables the SHA engine resource and loads five words from state_output into MMIO 0x38000020..30. Sets engine_control to 10 for continuation. Caller serializes hardware access and supplies the state words.
Accumulates wheel motion in 089ca550+0xc. Requires contact bit 0x40000000 in both samples, corrects wrap by 0x60, and filters noise. Contact transitions reset the consumed count at +0x10.
Sorts index entries using the native fields for order_mode. Mode 2 compares song shuffle ranks at entry+0x24. Brackets sorting with database allocation-update guards.

Reads a 16-bit length prefix and text following it, creates a temporary string and matches the 22 stock English preset names. Returns stored ID 100..121; null, empty and unknown names return 0. Destroys the temporary string on all matching and fallthrough paths.

Builds game paths. Arguments: output native string object, directory kind, game-identifier native string, storage-mode flag, relative-path C string. For kind 0, flag 0 selects iPod_Control/games_RO/<identifier>/<relative>; nonzero selects Resources/Games/games_RO/<identifier>/<relative>. Other kinds select gamedata_RW, gamestats_WO, or shared storage. Native strings use the two-word ABI.
Loads iPod_Control/Device/Preferences through the native file API after default initialization. Call at 080587ec occurs with filesystem available and before settings migration finishes.

Initializes preferences defaults, opens the native preferences path, reads at most the configured structure size, and updates two cached globals from the loaded fields. Closes the handle after reading; failed opens retain defaults.

Scans child atoms after the sample-entry header for sinf. Supports p608/drmi/drms/drmt headers of 0x20/0x66/0x34/0x3e bytes. Rebuilds the complete sinf atom in temporary storage and creates a media decryption context. Success stores slot mode 3/context and returns the decoded media format; failed creation retains the supplied format. Frees sinf storage and seeks to entry offset+0x18 after a found sinf. Unsupported formats return zero. Output on malformed/missing sinf follows the last atom type, so this is not a boolean success API.

Finds a game API module by its 32-byte name in the linked registry at 08a0fc88..08a1070c. Modules: Audio, Metadata, SoundEffect, AsyncFileIO, MemoryAlloc, InputEvents, Settings, OpenGLES, Users, DebugUtil, and miscTBD.
Returns arithmetic_shift_right_16(low32(sample_a*gain_a_q15 + sample_b*gain_b_q15)<<1). Speed overlap passes complementary weights. No saturation or wider accumulation is performed.
Maps raw wheel position to (((119 - (raw & 0xbfffffff)) * 8 / 3) & 0xff) | (raw & 0x40000000). Bit 30 is the contact flag used by InputWheel_AccumulateMotion.
Normalizes list order mode. Playback traversal mode 0x33 resolves to list+0xc8 when list+0x18c bit 0 is clear, or mode 2 when set. Mode 0 falls back to 1.
Arguments: serial context, byte count, buffer. Uses context port at +1; writes UART TX register +0x20 in chunks up to 16 bytes under a semaphore.
Maps stored IDs 100..121 to DSP presets 1..22; every other ID returns bypass preset 0. Flat (ID 107) maps to preset 8, so Flat and Off have distinct preset identities.
Reverse lookup of the 23 uint32 EQ IDs at 083e2568. r0=stored ID, r1=uint32 output pointer. Writes menu index, or -1 and returns -50 on failure.
Searches all 23 EQ IDs at 083e2568. Writes matching menu index and returns 0. Unknown ID writes 0xffffffff and returns -50; null output also returns -50.
Allocates capacity*4+0x14 bytes, records capacity and allocation size, and initializes count to zero. Returns NULL on allocation failure.

Programs SHA DMA mode=1 and length=64, writes engine control, polls the busy bit until clear, then writes the block address and sets continuation control=10. The visible poll precedes the address write; this leaf alone does not establish completion after that write. Does not update byte count.
Accepts logical port 1 and forwards buffer/count to UART_WriteBytes using context 0x08a7563c. Optional TX completion wait.
Copies the complete allocation using source+8 as its byte length. Returns NULL for a null source or allocation failure.
Walks the song record entry chain from record+0x24 through entry+0x28. Returns the first entry in the supplied list and subtree.
Accepts NULL cursor. Otherwise requires cursor.parent to belong to list and cursor.predecessor to be NULL, -1, or a child of that parent. Returns 1 when valid, else 0.
Waits for LCD_STATUS bit 1, delays, and selects the panel command interface. Panel types 0/1 use 8-bit commands; types 2/3 use 16-bit commands. Returns the previous LCD_CON value.
Waits for LCD_STATUS bit 1, delays, then writes LCD_CON at 0x38300000.

Returns negative, zero, or positive comparison. Field 0x1000 compares unsigned song shuffle ranks at +0x24 and places groups after songs; 0x8000 compares entry IDs. Other fields delegate to record/text comparison. The 64-bit field mask is passed on the stack after the unused r3 alignment slot.
Frees and clears cached indexes for order modes 1..48. Also invalidates the auxiliary cache for modes 6, 7, 9, and 24. Other modes are ignored.
Sets the 16-bit-command panel window using registers 0x210-0x213, cursor registers 0x200/0x201, and GRAM-write command 0x202. Restores the previous interface configuration.
Lazily builds list+0x3ac+4*order_mode. Mode 1 walks linked entries; other modes clone and sort that index. Returns 0 on success, -50 for an unsupported mode, or an allocation/build error.
Invalidates every supported order cache by visiting modes 1..48.
Compares entries using the context field sequence, falling back to entry ID (field 0x8000). After the first equal field, reverse_ties controls the sign of subsequent comparisons.
Returns the zero-terminated native field-mask sequence for an order mode, or NULL. Mode 2 selects shuffle-rank field 0x1000; mode 1 has a shuffle-enabled special case.

InputEvents export slot 0 via ARM branch 082bc194. ABI void(int32_t *delta, uint32_t *position_flags). Writes [089ca550+0xc] minus consumed count [+0x10], converts raw position [+0x20] through 080a7b40, advances the consumed count, and clears pending byte [+0]. Polling consumes the shared delta. Clockwise movement is positive, counterclockwise negative; faster movement produces larger deltas. Position bit 30 indicates contact.
Sets the 8-bit-command panel window with commands 0x2a and 0x2b, issues memory-write command 0x2c, and restores the previous interface configuration.
Returns the media-list object indexed by a nonnegative handle in the metadata service registry at +0x78/+0x7c. Returns NULL when the handle is outside the registry count.
Resolves an integer handle through the registry at GameMetadata service+0. Returns the library object or NULL.

Validates the game header, resolves imports by module name, checks 16-byte interface IDs and function counts, patches import stubs/table words, and copies up to five callbacks. Header: magic 0x70706165 (eapp), version +4 <=0x10001000, callback count +8 <=5, absolute import-list pointer +0x10 (zero allows no imports), callbacks +0x14. Import record: 32-byte name, interface ID +0x20, function count +0x30, next pointer +0x34, stubs +0x38, tail marker 0x29061968. OS registry tail marker: 0x13061973.
Returns 1 when selected slot 0..3 has a nonzero mode, otherwise 0. Out-of-range slot returns 0. Does not validate the FairPlay context pointer or key material.
Returns static four-slot crypto manager at 08ae47a8 through initialization guards. First initialized access clears slot mode bytes using MediaDRM_ClearSlotModes.
Clears mode bytes for four 0x28-byte slots and returns 0. Leaves context pointers, AES keys and IV bytes untouched; this is mode initialization rather than secure destruction.

For slot 0..3 in mode 3, invokes FairPlay_DecryptBuffer using that slot context. Slot 0 mode 4 instead calls locked AES with slot key/IV for bytes rounded down to 16, then copies the remaining 0..15 bytes. Other cases leave output untouched. Both decrypt return statuses are discarded here; caller must handle plain-data fallback separately.

Copies 0x28 bytes from track_records+track_index*0x60+0x38 into manager slot 0..3. Returns 0 on success and -1 for invalid slot. Copies pointers/key/IV as raw bytes without retaining or releasing a context; track index bounds belong to caller.

Scans game directories under iPod_Control/games_RO/ (mode 0) or Resources/Games/games_RO/ (mode 4). Builds Manifest.plist paths, checks existence through 080e9c00, reads metadata through 0806f4c8, and appends 0x50-byte game records. This path does not require a sync database. Stored function extent currently ends at 080f5ac7 before the scan loop; the current decompilation is incomplete. Confirm the continuation before using this as a callable patch ABI.
Gets the selected game identifier and storage mode, obtains the runtime singleton, and calls GameRuntime_RequestLaunch(runtime, nativeStringObject, mode, 0x66000003).
Builds manifest and signature paths. Call 080f9360 initializes the reader with the signature path in r3. This signed read follows the initial unsigned metadata read.
Iterates manifest file entries except selected executable, checks file sizes and invokes 082cc5e8 when Verify flag is set. Does not request a decryption context for these resource checks.

One-shot executable load: loader+0x58 blocks repeat attempts and is set after an attempted load, including failure. Loads manifest, verifies resources, selects the platform executable and reads it into caller backing_buffer bounded by capacity, returning byte count through output_bytes. Verify flag +0x18 requests the digest/context wrapper; DRM flag +0x19 requests .sinf metadata (<=0x4000 bytes) and in-place FairPlay decryption. Storage mode 4 can create a temporary game storage handle. Releases temporary metadata/context/handle and returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
Handles wheel input for the shared playback overlay. Switches the overlay to volume or brightness mode, adjusts the corresponding model value, and refreshes its timeout.
Initializes the timer passed as the second argument with the controller as its event recipient. Uses the current event queue when the fourth argument is null.
Builds version property 0x6402 from the numeric firmware version and platform suffix.
Uses volume controller at settings+0x88c. Returns true only when user-limit flag is set, user limit differs from regional ceiling, and requested volume is at least the user limit. No volume mutation.
Looks up a resource by type and ID, returning its data pointer and writing its byte length. For ROM-backed banks (kind 2), checks the override map at +0x18 before falling back to ResourceIndex_Find.
Copies or replaces a resource identified by type and ID. Arguments: bank, type, ID, data pointer, byte length. ROM-backed banks store the copy in their initialized override map.
Allocates the resource override map at bank+0x18. Called at 081c7410 before UI resource providers are constructed.

Continues the bank iterator started by ResourceBank_FirstResource. Returns resource data and writes ID/length, or NULL at exhaustion. Advances ROM iterator fields or releases the exhausted dynamic iterator.
Starts enumeration of one resource type in the bank. Returns the first data pointer and writes ID/length, or NULL if absent/empty. Stores iteration state in the bank for ResourceBank_NextResource.
Allocates and initializes a 0xb0-byte Silver controller for the supplied context, then attaches the shared selection model.
Calls controller vtable+0x114 with a nonempty handler name from the resolved event binding.
Copies the supplied item vector into the shared context-menu model, prepares its layout/controller, then attaches the resulting controller through owner vtable+0xd0.
Looks up the event binding, then its aliases. Returns 0 when neither resolves. For a binding, invokes its controller handler through 08129430 and runs its resource actions.
Allocates a 0xec-byte Silver controller with a transition addon at +0xb0. Initializes the supplied context, transition data, flags and mode.
Prefixes the supplied native string with controller. and posts event subtype 0x2a to the controller's event queue.
Creates the provider and hides MainMenu_List_Debug (0x0dad01a1). Instruction 0812ad24 supplies visibility value 0.
Handles ShowSetting_EQ and HandleEQ; argument 0xdeadbeef checks availability without executing. The native list produces menu indices, distinct from stored IDs.
Recognizes ShowSetting_EQ and HandleEQ and invokes the corresponding handler. Argument 0xdeadbeef probes support without executing. Returns 1 for recognized actions and 0 otherwise.
Reads SLst for the screen ID at +0x04. Constructs each layout from its resource ID and the low byte of the record field at +0x04, then associates the layout with this screen.
Initializes the screen definition with the supplied resource ID. Optionally loads its layouts, then reads the controller class name from SCST. Aborts if SCST is missing.

Returns static diagnostic WAV service using initialization guards; first initialized access calls 0813e3b0 to start its worker infrastructure. PCM processing calls this around capture setup and the append stub.
Clears capture-active byte at service+4 and tail-calls 080cfe50 with the global worker synchronization object. Called after the PCM diagnostic frame budget is exhausted.

Resets the embedded writer at service+8, configures filename/channels/rate/bits through 08156618, resets another service through 0815d018, sets active byte +4 and stores format at +0x38/+0x3c/+0x40. This setup exists even though the PCM append entry is a no-op in this image.

Immediate BX LR in stock 2.0.4. Caller passes PCM base and frames*4 bytes, but this entry writes nothing and leaves capture data untouched. Do not use this call as evidence of a functioning PCM recording path.
Finds a resource type and ID in a version-3 ROM resource index. Returns data-base plus the stored resource offset and writes its byte length. Type and sparse-ID lookups use binary search.
Branch thunk to NativeString_InitEmpty at 0826c568; initializes the two-word native string and returns its address.
Returns the volume-controller singleton, allocating a 0x8c-byte object and calling 0815565c on first use. Initialization loads preferences and configures the secondary-output ramp timer.
Returns user-limit field +0x58 without checking the enable flag. Volume vtable slot +0x88; Settings compares it with the regional ceiling and requested volume.

Clamps requested limit between floor(regional_ceiling/10) and regional_ceiling via vtable+0x60. Stores +0x58, writes preference through 0805ce28, then reapplies requested volume +0x54 with notifications disabled.
Loads saved volume through 0804b24c into +0x54 and saved user limit through 0804b164; applies that limit with virtual method +0x84. Applying it also reapplies current volume.
Returns user-limit enable byte +0x52. Volume vtable slot +0x8c; effective-limit and UI warning paths use it to select the user cap.
Lazily caches regional ceiling: 0xd8 when Platform_HasRegionalVolumeLimit returns nonzero, otherwise 0x100. Subsequent calls use the cached word. Values are volume units, not PCM sample gains.
Returns whether Platform_HasRegionalVolumeLimit is nonzero. Used through volume vtable +0x80; does not return a numeric ceiling.
Returns user limit +0x58 when flag +0x52 is nonzero; otherwise returns the regional ceiling. Dispatches through vtable +0x8c flag query, +0x88 user-limit getter and +0x60 regional getter.

If byte +0x53 is clear, sets it and reapplies requested volume through vtable +0x54 with notify=0. Already enabled is a no-op. The volume apply method uses this flag to schedule the secondary-output ramp.
If byte +0x53 is set, clears it and reapplies requested volume through vtable +0x54 with notify=0. Already disabled is a no-op. The apply method then writes unity 0x100 to secondary output.
Sets mute flag at volume+0x51 and sends level 0 to audio outputs 0 and 1. Retains requested volume and user limit for restoration.
Clears mute flag +0x51 and tail-calls the shared reapply path at 081552a0, which invokes vtable+0x54 with stored requested volume +0x54 and notify=0.
Returns requested-volume field +0x54. Vtable slot +0x5c; value precedes the floating multiplier and differs from the saved applied-volume preference.

Handles event kind 0x0f only when its timer pointer matches volume+0x60. Computes target=(user_limit<<8)/regional_ceiling for output 1; raises current value by 5 and reschedules while target-current>4, otherwise applies target. Returns 1 for its timer event, 0 otherwise. Event and payload must be valid.

Clears mute flag +0x51; clamps to user limit +0x58, applies floating multiplier +0x5c, then clamps again. With flag +0x52 clear, requested-volume storage +0x54 is clamped to regional ceiling; otherwise it stores the user-limited value. Updates output 0; output 1 gets unity 0x100 or timer ramp according to +0x53. A global override forces 0xf4. Optionally notifies listeners and marks changed applied-volume preference dirty.

Initializes the volume controller and event/listener base, installs vtable 08987c2c, initializes its embedded +0x34 object, route byte +0x50=2, unmuted state, user-cap flag=1, multiplier=1.0 and secondary-ramp flag=0. Loads saved preferences, optionally applies 70 percent of user limit when the startup flag is set, then initializes the +0x60 ramp timer with interval 10. Returns the controller.

Returns 0 after dispatch: selector 0 dereferences Q15 gain, 1 passes the speed-setting payload, 2 dereferences EQ preset, 3 calls the empty byte-property handler at 0818c310. Returns -1 for context 0xffffffff or unknown selector. Recognized payloads must be valid pointers; context null is not rejected.

Polls IRAM output status against four times a service limit while the stop flag is clear, sleeping 10 units between queries. Acquires queue-0 read descriptor, sets its frame count to zero if stopping, and forwards its seven words to service 22007fe4. Ownership is later released by Audio_ProcessEffectsAndOutput. This path can block.

Obtains effects context through IRAM service. On failure writes context 0xffffffff and returns -1. On changed rate/channels, polls output status with 10-unit sleeps and waits for queued audio duration before reconfiguration. Reads rate/bits/channels at descriptor+4/+8/+0xc and frames at +0x28; sets service/source format and input frames, returns 0. Ignores ConfigureSourceFormat failure.
Appends a 12-byte context-menu item {ID, action-name pointer, flags} to the vector, growing its storage when full.
Registers the native Settings controller classes with the controller factory registry, supplying normal and wrapped constructors.
Queries stored EQ ID through player vtable +0xa4 and converts it with EQ_SettingsIdToMenuIndex. Returns menu index or -1 if the stored ID is unknown.

Reads two order flags from playback list +0x64. Returns 0 when first flag is clear; otherwise 1 when second is clear or 2 when set. Local temporary words in the original decompile do not represent extra caller arguments.
Returns player byte +0x93f, the active On-The-Go playback flag. No list validation or normalization is performed.

Checks index against low-16-bit preset count from preferences. If valid, sends setting request 0x6063/0x6000 with a four-byte index payload and player callback context. Returns whether index was in range; setting application occurs through the request machinery.

Requires a valid list, clear restriction byte +0x941 and an allowed context. Resolves order into two stored flags, preserves current entry identity across reordering, updates cached index and prepared entry metadata, emits change notifications, then rebinds source +0x948. Can invalidate audio-player caches through source assignment.

Locks the mutex at +0xa4c, queries MediaTrack_GetPosition for active track +0x54, then unlocks. Returns zero when no active track exists. Position units come from the selected backend and are not independently established here.
Appends a selection to playback-list wrapper this+0x60, using the supplied browsing context or this+0x9a8. Primary vtable slot +0x128; called by OnTheGo_AddSelection when this+0x93f is set.
Returns the current playback-list index at +0x5c, used by preparation and transition code to resolve an entry. Does not validate the list, take a lock or convert the index to a media ID.

Temporarily selects the playback list and browse mode 5, adds track_index to On-The-Go, then restores browse state. Returns true on error and false on success (the wrapped legacy status is inverted into a boolean).

Under player mutex +0xa4c, subtracts current position from duration returned by active MediaItem vtable +0xa0. Returns zero for no active track or position beyond duration. Both values use backend position units; no conversion to samples or seconds occurs.
Branch thunk to Audio_SetPlaybackSource; forwards source to audio backend vtable+0x5c.
Returns state byte +0x93d. Companion predicates test 0 stopped, 1 playing and 2 paused; dispatcher may expose a separate predicted state for queued commands.
Handles player event 0: advances current or prepared track state. When +0x58 is empty, resolves the next entry, creates its track object and queues audio command 2.

Finds the next playable entry in the current playback list or returns NULL. Traversal flags control direction and special grouping; bit 7 selects reverse traversal. Optional output is cleared first and set when the playback order changes with multiple entries. Loop detection prevents cycling forever.
Returns playback-list +0x18d bit 2 normalized to 0/1; invalid list returns false. Game module exposes this independently of the main shuffle-enabled bit.
Resolves order 3 through the browse-context preference. Writes enabled=(order!=0) and albums=(order==2). Does not mutate the playback list.
Under player lock +0xa4c, finalizes and frees the prepared track object at +0x58, then clears the pointer.

Creates a playback list in the browsing context database at +0xf60. Registers its event listener, sets list+0x18c bit 7, and copies the repeat mode. Creation flags are 0: flat entries and duplicates allowed.

For a valid list and non-stopped player, updates the current item, finishes/clears the prepared track, sets state +0x93d to 0, queues worker stop and waits for queue-empty plus worker-idle. Resets associated playback services and publishes notifications. Can block; unsuitable for a PCM callback.

Stores EQ ID at +0x94d, takes player mutex +0xa4c, and refreshes the active stream through 08173288 when list and prepared track are valid. Releases mutex before returning. The stored ID is distinct from menu index and DSP preset.
Returns whether playback-state byte +0x93d equals 2. The pause request path stores this after queueing worker command 3, so the state can precede hardware completion.
Returns whether playback-state byte +0x93d equals 1. A control-state query with no lock or DSP call; it does not independently prove audio hardware is currently producing samples.
Returns whether playback-state byte +0x93d is zero. Raw ARM implements an unsigned 1-state subtraction with carry handling. Does not wait for the worker or test list validity.
Returns requested playback speed at +0x950, with 1000 denoting normal speed. Does not query whether a queued request or DSP transition has completed.
Resolves current_index, finds the next playable entry, and maps it back to playback order. Returns -1 when unavailable or when active repeat restrictions reject a wrap.

Accepts 500..2000 (1000 normal); rejected values leave state unchanged. Under mutex +0xa4c stores speed at +0x950 and calls 08172d3c when a valid list/prepared track exists, then releases mutex. Can block, so this is a control-side entry rather than an audio callback.

Lazily allocates and constructs TPodMediaPlayer when singleton pointer at global+4 is null, caches it and returns it. This body has no explicit lock or allocation failure check. Constructor initializes playback lists, settings, timers and worker-facing state.
Reads repeat preference from playback-list object at +0x64. Stored mode 1 maps to API mode 2 (all), stored 2 maps to API mode 1 (one), other values map to 0. Game bridge caches this API value.

Dispatches work event ID at event+4: 0 prepares next track; 1/2 advance with flags 3 (1 adds an outer mutex); 3 runs the alternate track transition; 4 flushes pending preferences/library work. Event 15 forwards its 0xd00 payload to player vtable +0x1d4. Unhandled work delegates to the base event handler. Returns handled/result status.

Holds player mutex +0xa4c and finds the next playable entry using selection_flags|0x80. No active track or exhausted selection returns false; exhaustion also stops playback. Handles source/list changes, saves old position, installs the next item, and resumes or queues a paused load according to player state. Releases temporary MediaItems and returns true after transition setup.
Returns true only for valid playback list and stored uint16 repeat mode +0x184 equal to 1. Invalid list returns false. API repeat setter maps repeat-all mode 2 to this stored value.
Returns true only for valid playback list and stored uint16 repeat mode +0x184 equal to 2. Invalid list returns false. API repeat setter maps repeat-one mode 1 to this stored value.

Requires a valid playback list, clear restriction byte +0x940 and an allowed playback context. Converts API modes 0/1/2 to stored 0/2/1; mode 3 resolves the global repeat preference first. Writes list preference then queues/notifies a player change event. Unsupported values are not locally rejected after the gate.
Returns playback-list +0x18c bit 0, or false for invalid list. This reads stored order state rather than the game bridge requested-order cache.

Under player lock +0xa4c, finalizes and releases the current track at +0x54, clears that pointer, and processes pending transition flags at +0x93c. Returns the mutex-release status. The separate prepared track at +0x58 is handled by MediaPlayer_ClearPreparedTrack.

For track states 3/4, reads requested speed from track->settings(+0x20)+8 and accepts inclusive 500..2000. Sends enabled=1 plus speed to 0x081a6110, except 1000 sends enabled=0 and value=0. Invalid range or inactive state returns without changing DSP configuration.

Selects position source by track state byte +0. States 3/4 query the audio service; state 5 uses media metadata +0x5c or +0x64 after validity checks; states 0/1/2/6 delegate to source vtable +0x1c with embedded MediaItem +4. Unknown states return zero. Position units are backend-defined.
Advances track state 1 to 2 or 3 to 4 on player event 0.

Only acts for track states 3/4. Converts settings ID at track->settings(+0x20)+5 to a DSP preset. Unless global ID is Flat (107), a nonzero per-track EQ ID overrides it. Sends the selected DSP preset through 0x081a5bdc. Off, Flat, stored IDs and DSP preset numbers are distinct.
For state 0, queues audio command 2 with the track index and sets state 1.

Transitions between layout instances and applies their component bindings. SLst byte +0x08 forces a refresh when selecting the current layout again. Five register/stack inputs are visible, but the exact selection/transition flag contract is still unresolved; retain the inferred signature until caller analysis establishes it.

Applies the selected resource table to a template instance. VCrv supplies the parent rectangle and SSin +0x12 controls scrolling; binding tables update child views and item tables. The six-input ABI includes caller-owned binding state; its detailed parameter types remain provisional.
Resolves the entering transition from SSin +0x0c or the template defaults for the supplied layout transition. A record value of -1 selects the defaults.
Resolves the leaving transition from SSin +0x0e or the template defaults for the supplied layout transition. A record value of -1 selects the defaults.
Allocates and constructs a 0x24-byte resource-block list for the source-descriptor resource ID using the shared provider. Caller owns the returned list.
Copies the first 12-byte source descriptor from the selected resource and destroys the temporary block list. An empty list yields two zero words and type byte 6.
Allocates a 12-byte descriptor {byte_length, metadata, data} and appends its pointer to the list vector. Sets the borrowed-data flag; the payload remains externally owned.

Initializes the list resource selectors and flags. Unless deferred, loads the resource when the descriptor vector is empty: reads a block count, wraps each payload as borrowed data, and aligns the next block to four bytes.
Constructs the 0x24-byte block-list object and its descriptor vector, then initializes/loads the selected resource through ResourceBlockList_Load. Returns list.
Looks up the registered Silver selection-model service and requests its shared model.

On eq_cache == -1, queries player vtable +0xb4 and caches its EQ menu index. Returns cached value thereafter; snapshot invalidates it. Unknown stored EQ IDs can produce -1 through the player conversion.
Lazily fills order_cache from player vtable +0x7c when -1, then returns low byte. Player maps stored order flags to 0/1/2; later queued changes use this cache before completion.

Requires a valid player list at player+0x60. Stores requested EQ index in cache, allocates command 66000012 with a 4-byte payload and queues it through dispatcher+4. Returns false for invalid list, otherwise true. Does not locally bound index or wait for application.

With a valid playback list, caches order low byte and queues command 6600000f with one payload byte. Invalid list is a no-op. Player implementation changes list order while preserving the current entry.

Builds a 16-byte command payload. When use_record is zero, clones nonnull selection data into an owned buffer; otherwise carries the record pointer. Queues command 66000014 with mode/option. Consumer 0817e66c frees the cloned selection; record pointer lifetime belongs to caller. No completion result is returned.

Returns min(requested volume, regional ceiling) * 255 / regional ceiling using unsigned integer division. Queries volume vtable +0x5c/+0x60. Excludes the floating gain multiplier; division remainder in r1 is incidental.

Clamps unsigned volume to 255, scales it by regional ceiling / 255, then calls volume apply vtable +0x54 with notify=0. Bridge pointer is unused. User-limit and multiplier handling occur in the apply method.

Returns static game Audio bridge through C++ initialization guard. Bridge +0 holds the normal MediaPlayer and +4 its command dispatcher; module wrappers call this before their service methods. Guard initialization may block.

Maps index through EQ_MenuIndexToSettingsId and applies the resulting low-byte settings ID via MediaPlayer vtable +0xa0. No local index bounds check; caller must supply 0..22. This is the direct apply path rather than the queued bridge setter.

Marks playback_changed. For serialized selection, resolves a media record using option, frees the owned selection on both resolution failure and success, and loads a temporary MediaItem through player +0x120. For direct-record mode, loads a nonnull record without freeing it. Destroys temporary MediaItem after dispatch.
Returns effective volume limit * 255 / regional ceiling using volume vtable +0x64/+0x60. Effective limit chooses user cap or regional ceiling according to enable flag. Return is quotient in r0.
On gain_cache == -40000, queries volume vtable +0x6c and caches the result. Returns cached signed control value; setter clamps to -32767..32767. Physical units are unresolved.
Returns dispatcher predicted playback state through 080f577c. Dispatcher +0x140 overrides the current player state when not -1, so this can reflect a queued command before playback changes.
Clamps signed gain to -32767..32767, stores gain_cache and queues command 66000025 with four payload bytes. Does not check playback-list validity. Physical units and later conversion are unresolved.
Stores bridge byte +0xd. RestorePlayerSettings tests for value exactly 1 before resetting the modified playback list; this setter does not normalize other byte values.

Captures repeat mode, playback order and EQ menu index from player vtable +0x6c/+0x7c/+0xb4 into saved fields +8/+9/+a. Invalidates requested caches to -1, clears speed cache and change/restore flags, and sets gain cache to -40000 sentinel. Returns true.

If playback_changed is 1, resets the modified playback list. Restores saved repeat/order, restores speed to 1000 when a nondefault speed was cached, and conditionally restores EQ when restore_eq is set and index changed. Resets nonzero cached gain through volume service, refreshes preferences and submits the default output configuration to IRAM. Can invoke player synchronization and asynchronous setting work.

Returns speed_cache, refreshing it from player vtable +0xdc when (cache & (global byte 089ca3a4 - 1)) == 0. Cache uses 1000 for normal speed. Preserves the exact gate because the global byte meaning is unresolved.

Accepts inclusive 500..2000 and requires a valid playback list. Caches requested speed, queues command 66000013 with a 4-byte payload, clears global byte 089ca3a4 and returns true. Invalid range/list returns false. Units use 1000 for normal playback.
Lazily fills repeat_cache from player vtable +0x6c when -1, then returns its low byte. API modes are 0 off, 1 repeat-one, 2 repeat-all; storage uses the opposite 1/2 mapping.

With a valid playback list, caches mode low byte and queues command 6600000e with one payload byte. Invalid list is a no-op. Queueing does not establish that the player accepted or applied the requested mode.

Initializes player and dispatcher pointers at +0/+4; clears saved setting bytes +8..d, initializes caches +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 to -1, speed cache +0x1c to 0 and gain cache +0x20 to -40000. Returns bridge. Snapshot/restore methods later populate the saved settings.
Stores the low byte of r1 at effects context r0+0, then returns.
Tail-calls EQ_SetDspPreset on the embedded EQ at context+0x18034. Presets above 22 become bypass 0; changing the preset reloads coefficients and clears filter history.
Stores the nominal input frame count at context+0x2a174. Stream assignment supplies descriptor+0x28; Audio_EstimateOutputFrameCount passes this through each enabled effect.

Accepts 8000..48000 Hz, 8/16 bits and 1/2 channels; returns 1 on success, 0 on invalid input. Writes destination fields progressively, so failure can leave rate/bits changed. Recomputes converter ratio and enable state, then calls all three effect sample-rate methods. Context offsets: output +2a184/+188/+18c; source +2a178/+17c/+180.
Ignores null setting. Otherwise tail-calls the embedded speed effect at context+0x180ec with mode=setting[0] and signed 16-bit value at setting+2. Audio property selector 1 reaches this wrapper.

Starts with context+0x2a174 input frames. For each enabled effect, calls vtable+0x18 with (effect, current_frames, &current_frames), then writes the final count. Converter adds a safety frame; EQ leaves the count unchanged.

Runs enabled converter, EQ and speed stages via vtable+0x1c, propagating PCM pointer and frame count. Releases source buffer through Audio_ReleasePCMReadBuffer when first replaced, otherwise after output submission. Applies Q15 gain to stereo S16; diagnostic setup/frame-budget code calls an empty append stub at 0813e3fc. Forwards r1 and four opaque stack words to IRAM 22006f40. PCM hook 0818c4b4: r6=base, r4=frames, r9=context; check destination format before custom DSP.

Post-effects handoff: r6=PCM buffer base, r4=stereo frame count, r9=effects context. Q15 gain loop advances [sp+0x14], not r6. Output rate is context+0x2a184; guard destination bits/channels at +0x2a188/+18c before treating samples as stereo S16. Displaced str r4,[sp,#0x44]; str r6,[sp,#0x40] precede 0802d100 and output thunk 0802d220 -> IRAM 22006f40. Incoming IRAM veneer: file 0x41e0, target literal 0818c320 at 0x41e4.

Post-effects PCM handoff: r6=buffer base, r4=stereo frame count, r9=effects context. Q15 gain advances the stack-local cursor, retaining r6. Output service is 0802d220 -> IRAM 22006f40. Incoming veneer: osos.bin file 0x41e0, target literal 0818c320 at 0x41e4. The diagnostic call at 0818c494 passes frames*4 bytes to the immediate-return stub 0813e3fc.

Accepts 8000..48000 Hz, 8/16 bits (0 becomes 16), and 1/2 channels. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure; invalid later fields can leave earlier fields changed. Stores source format, recalculates converter phase/ratio and bypass, and stores the mono stride flag at context+0xd. Called by stream assignment even when formats match.

Stores gain at context+0x2a170, clamping unsigned values >=0x8000 to 0x7fff. PCM processing multiplies each stereo S16 sample by gain then arithmetic-shifts 15; 0x7fff bypasses multiplication. Property selector 0 reaches this setter.

Constructs converter at +4, three-band EQ at +0x18034 and speed effect at +0x180ec. Stores their pointers at +0x2a190, disables each through vtable+8, clears stream_active, sets gain 0x7fff and source/output defaults to 44100 Hz, 16-bit stereo. Returns context. Converter constructor only sets its vtable; later format setup initializes its ratio/history fields.
Returns route code 3 when the stored route byte at global+1 is nonzero, otherwise 0. Hardware meaning of these route codes is not established by this accessor.
Rebuilds menu-item mappings and provider subscriptions. ITEM records with byte +0x64 equal to zero are omitted from the visible-index vector and visible count.

Replaces the current resource block list when table_id changes, resets the optional view, and rebuilds visible items. ID zero selects the default table at menu_list+0x2c. Returns 1 when rebuilt, else 0.
Enumerates resources of resource_type and registers each item payload in the global map keyed by its ID at payload+0x30. Destroys temporary descriptor lists after each resource.
Looks up the ITEM record by item ID, updates its visibility byte at +0x64, and sends LitE/None notifications. Menu-list rebuilding omits records whose visibility byte is zero.

Passes source to active audio-player service at global+4 via vtable +0x5c. The selected implementation owns source replacement and cache invalidation; this wrapper performs neither reference checks nor buffer reset itself.
Enumerates View resources, reads each matching TMLT record, and constructs templates selected by the owner flag at +0x108. Finalizes the template collection after enumeration.

Loads pending 16-byte sample-table entries from reader+0x1bc in the requested range after dividing start/duration by 10. Mode byte reader+0x1f0 == 3 uses crypto slot 2, requires two scratch objects and packet size <=1024, validates cdat at decrypted bytes 4..7, and copies payload after the 8-byte header. Invalid encrypted packets clear entry data/size; plain packets read payload directly. Advances the table cursor and returns 1. Original time units and minimum-size validation belong to further caller tracing.

Selects a track through reader+0x1b0 and fills pending 0x50-byte sample entries in the requested range, with start/duration divided by 10. Track mode +0x10 == 3 reads encrypted bytes through a 1024-byte stack workspace and crypto slot 3; other modes read directly. Calls 081bdbe4 to validate/process each entry and copies four 16-bit track metadata values into entry+0x21. Returns 1 on completion, 3 for missing track or failed processing. This body has no explicit sample-size check against its stack workspace; upstream bounds remain unverified.
Applies twice the signed button step to the shared volume, bounds the request by the available maximum, and notifies listeners.
Applies the controller's volume step at +0xb8 and restarts its repeat timer at +0xb0 with a 125 ms interval.
Builds the UI resource-provider chain. Gets the default resource bank, initializes its override map at call site 081c7410, then constructs and registers providers.
Loads device option marker files; _enable_options gates most diagnostic options.

Loads native debug marker-file options. Checks the enable-options gate before loading the extended option set; always loads the surrounding baseline options. Some readers update logging and other subsystem state.
Checks iPod_Control/Device/_enable_logging and enables the native event logger.
Checks iPod_Control/Device/_enable_logging, stores the result in debug-options byte +0x0a, and applies it to the event-log singleton.
Checks iPod_Control/Device/_enable_options and stores the result at 0x089caf45.
Checks iPod_Control/Device/_enable_options, stores its presence at debug-options byte +1, and returns that result. DebugOptions_Load uses it to gate the extended option readers.
Checks iPod_Control/Device/_usb_swap_configs; 0x089caf60 inverts the USB configuration-mode argument.
Checks the USB-swap-configurations marker under iPod_Control/Device and stores its presence in debug-options byte +0x1c.

Allocates a 12-byte command {id=1, index}, enqueues it, ensures the thread and signals worker+0x20. Worker calls audio load with (index,1,0); the caller may then queue a position command. Returns before completion.

Lazily allocates and initializes the 0x28-byte audio command worker and stores its singleton pointer. Does not start its thread; first queue submission calls EnsureThread. No synchronization around first allocation is visible here.

Polls until the command queue is empty and worker byte +0x26 is nonzero. Sleeps with argument 100 between unsuccessful polls, with no timeout. Queue emptiness alone is insufficient because the worker clears idle while applying a drained batch.

If started byte +0x25 is clear, creates the thread with entry 0x081d41fc and then sets the byte. Entry obtains the singleton and enters AudioWorker_Run. Uses a 0x8000 creation argument and does not inspect a creation result. Must run outside real-time PCM processing.

Persistent worker loop. Sets idle +0x26 before signal wait, clears it on wake, drains/frees queued commands, then applies a coalesced batch. IDs 0/1 load playing/paused, 2 prepare, 3/4 pause/resume, 5 position, 6 playback option, 7 stop, 8/9 special controls. Command 8 suppresses later queued commands in that batch and takes priority over 9 and ordinary work. Stop clears accumulated ordinary work; later commands may re-enable it. Returns to signal wait after application; no normal exit path.

Allocates command 7, enqueues it, ensures thread startup and signals worker+0x20. While draining, stop clears pending load/pause/resume/seek/preparation flags already accumulated; later commands can set them again. Worker calls 0x081a6064(1). Use WaitUntilIdle when completion is required.

Allocates command 3, enqueues it, ensures thread startup and signals worker+0x20. Worker makes pause/resume mutually exclusive within the drained batch and applies pause through 0x081a60b0. Player state is updated separately by the caller.

Allocates command 4, enqueues it, ensures thread startup and signals worker+0x20. Worker makes pause/resume mutually exclusive within the drained batch and applies resume through 0x081a60d4. Returns before the audio service completes.

Allocates a 12-byte command {id=0, index}, enqueues it, ensures the thread exists and signals worker+0x20. Worker coalesces the batch and calls audio load with (index,1,1). Returns before playback completion.

Allocates a 12-byte command {id=2, index}, enqueues it, ensures the thread and signals worker+0x20. Worker invokes audio load with (index,0,1) after other pending controls. Queueing allocates and does not wait for preparation.

Initializes the 0x28-byte worker: queue/vtable, queue lock at +0xc, wait structure at +0x14, signal at +0x20, started byte +0x25=0 and idle byte +0x26=1. Returns storage. Construction alone does not spawn the thread.
Returns the controller factory registry singleton, constructing it on first use.

Creates a progress-bar view from the resource description in argument 4 (r3). Style 6 uses the alternate factory; other styles allocate a 0xfc-byte object, with styles 8/9 selecting the specialized constructor. The decoded constructor description is passed as argument 5 to ProgressBar_Initialize.
Loads and merges TEVT tables for the layout instances, SEVT for this layout ID, and CEVT for the associated controller into the event table at +0x38. Aborts when a required table is missing.
Loads the layout event tables on first access, sets the initialized flag at +0x54, and returns the merged table at +0x38.
Reads SLyt for this layout ID. Each group references an SSin resource and a byte at record offset +0x04. Stores the instance records in the layout and group collections.
Returns the layout transition byte stored at +0x0c.
Constructs a layout with its resource ID, transition byte, and SLst record pointer. Loads its component groups and initializes lazy event loading.
Frames caller bytes as HID reports with a two-byte header and sends them on endpoint 0x83 via 0x08289aac. Requires active interface flag at context+0x14.

Linearly interpolates interleaved S16 stereo into converter+0x30 with saturation. Uses persistent phase +0x24, Q16 source/output step +0x28 and previous L/R +0x2c/+0x2e across blocks. Writes emitted frame count, retains the final input frame and residual phase. Requires nonzero input frames, nonzero step and enough internal buffer capacity.
Copies each contiguous mono S16 input sample to both L/R channels in converter+0x30. Writes output_frames=frames. Caller must fit the internal output buffer.

Interpolates contiguous mono S16 with persistent Q16 phase/step, saturates and duplicates into stereo output at +0x30. Retains the last mono sample at +0x2c and residual phase at +0x24. Requires nonzero input frames and step; writes output count.

Stores source/output rates at +0xc/+0x10, clears phase +0x24 and sets step +0x28 to round((source_rate/output_rate)*65536) through software float helpers. Does not clear previous samples at +0x2c/+0x2e. Caller must supply a nonzero output rate.

Copies every other S16 input sample to both stereo channels in converter+0x30. Input stride is four bytes per mono frame; output_frames=frames. Selected when source_channels=1 and mono_in_stereo_stride=1.
Compares source/output rate, bit depth and channel count; calls effect vtable+8 with 1 if any differ, otherwise 0. Does not compare the mono stride flag or reset conversion history.

Interpolates mono S16 carried at four-byte input stride, saturates and duplicates to stereo at +0x30. Retains final strided sample at +0x2c and Q16 phase at +0x24. Requires nonzero input frames and step; writes output count.

Writes ((input_frames << 16) / step_q16) + 1 using integer division. Used as converter vtable+0x18 sizing method. The shift is 32-bit; valid callers must keep it in range and initialize a nonzero step.

Zero frames writes only output_frames=0. Equal-rate nonmono input returns the original pointer/count. Otherwise duplicates mono or linearly resamples stereo/mono to internal buffer +0x30; mono flag +9 selects two- versus four-byte source stride. Implemented paths load S16 despite stored 8-bit format options; this routine has no general 8-bit conversion branch.
Installs converter vtable 0x0898f188 and returns the same pointer in r0. Other converter fields are initialized by surrounding storage/setup paths.
Handles HandleMenuSelection by reading the selected action string, dismissing the popup, finding its owner, and posting the action through vtable+0x124.

Internal fall-through block of ContextMenu_DispatchAction at 081dd8f0, entered after acquiring the context-menu model. Uses the parent frame and preserved controller in r5. Resolves the selected action, dismisses the popup, and posts it to the owner. Treat this as an internal block, not an independently callable ABI.
Prefixes the selected action with contextualMenu. and queues a type-0x2a string event to the owning controller.

Creates a template object for the resource ID in the fifth argument. Reads its TMLT record, builds the parent and child objects, applies layout and color fields, and returns the template object. Aborts if the TMLT record is missing or empty. Six inputs are present; resource ID is argument 5, while the remaining factory/context types are still provisional.
r1 is menu index 0..22. Looks up preview resource from 089cc500[index*2+1]; stock bound checked.
Returns the preview resource for EQ menu indices 0..22 from the odd word of each table pair. Returns the shared empty value outside that range. model is unused by this lookup.
r1 is a menu index 0..22, not a stored settings ID. Looks up string resource from 089cc500[index*2]; returns empty string out of range.

Returns the localized name resource for EQ menu indices 0..22 from the even word of each table pair. Returns the shared empty value outside that range. The index is the menu position; model is unused.
Invokes the model virtual method at vtable offset +0x58 with arguments 0x2a2a2a2a and 0x8928. Called by Settings_HandleAction for ShowSetting_Legal.
Loads settings-service pointer at model+0x378 then tail-calls 081670d4. r1 is UI/menu index, passed through property 0x6063. Settings_SetEQPreset translates that index to the stored ID.
Passes menu_index by address to the selection model at +0x378 through vtable+0xd8, using event selectors 0x6063/0x6000.
Closes the controller when mode is zero; otherwise selects and activates the playback screen for the current media.
Returns the shared Now Playing model, allocating its 0x3bc-byte object on first use.
Adjusts the shared volume controller by twice the signed input delta, clamps to the available range, and applies the volume with listener notification.
Clears display suppression and cached media data, then restarts the volume-display timer when playback permits it.
Sets the model's automatic-display suppression byte at +0xbc and stops its volume-display timer at +0xc0.
Checks playback state, then opens the media now-playing controller when the current controller permits an overlay; otherwise refreshes the playback model volume-display timer.

Destroys previous source via vtable +4 when nonnull and different, stores source at player+0x18, and sets cache-invalidated byte +0x67 even when pointer is unchanged. The next track-load path consumes this flag.
Branch thunk to UI_GetControllerRegistry at 081d4b48; returns the lazily constructed controller factory registry.

Returns the static PCM double-buffer manager using a C++ initialization guard. On the initialized path, sets the one-time access flag before returning. PCM producer/consumer functions use queue index 0.

For both slots, zeroes min(frames*4,0x4000) bytes when the slot has a PCM pointer, then clears its frame count. Keeps pointers, slot states and producer/consumer indices. Slot base is manager+queue*0x38+slot*0x1c+8.

Selects the current producer slot. If preserve_pointer is zero, installs fixed PCM storage 08adc7a8 or 08ae07a8 according to slot index. Returns its pointer through pcm, marks slot state 2 and returns 0. Does not wait for slot availability or advance the index.

Writes frame count and three opaque metadata words into current producer slot; nonnull pcm replaces its pointer. Marks state 3 and advances producer index modulo two. r2 and the second stack word are unused here. No lock or capacity check is performed.
Clears both slot pointers, states and frame counts for the selected queue. Leaves producer/consumer indices and trailing metadata unchanged.

Selects current consumer slot and writes descriptor+4 PCM pointer, +8 frames, +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 metadata. Marks state 4 without advancing the consumer index. Descriptor words +0 and +0xc remain caller-owned; the loaded slot state is not checked.
Binds two fixed 0x4000-byte buffers at 08adc7a8 and 08ae07a8. Marks each slot available (state 1) and clears frame counts. Leaves index and metadata fields unchanged.

Optionally calls IRAM 22005018 then 2200530c, marks current consumer slot available (state 1), and advances its index modulo two. Effects processing calls this once when replacing the source buffer, or after output submission when retaining it.

Initializes queue 0 producer/consumer indices and both slots: null PCM, state 0, zero frames/metadata, final metadata word 0xffffffff. Binds the two fixed buffers, making them available. Returns manager. The apparent outer decompiler loop executes once.
Lazily creates image handles for the thumb and the filled and unfilled bar segments using the view model and configured resource IDs.
Reads the bound range from the model, updates the minimum, maximum and current value, and invalidates the view when the range changes.
Draws the filled and unfilled bar segments within the supplied clip, then draws the optional thumb and secondary markers.

Initializes the progress-bar base view and imports style and image-resource IDs from the fifth argument. Clears the cached image pointers and secondary-value state. ARM instructions forward r0-r3 plus stack argument 5 to base constructor 08120a74 and return its r0 object pointer. The base constructor parameter meanings remain provisional.
Destroys the thumb, marker and bar image handles, then destroys the base progress view.
Within Files (token 7), handles DRM token 3 -> entry+0x19 and Verify token 0x14 -> entry+0x18. Token names in table 083f1910.
Shows the volume layout when needed and applies the signed wheel delta at event offset +0x0c to the controller's playback model.
Handles next-track input, refreshes controller/overlay state, and delegates to playback or the alternate media path. Returns 1 after handling.
Reads the selected row from the shared selection model. For a valid selection, maps it through vtable+0x130 and invokes the add-to-OTG handler at +0x13c.
Reads the selected row from the shared selection model. For a valid selection, maps it through vtable+0x130 and invokes the context-menu builder at +0x148.
Adds the current playback index through the player OTG method, refreshes the temporary list model, and releases it. Returns 1.

Builds context-menu items for the current media, including eligible album/Genius/OTG or audiobook-speed actions and Cancel. Shows the menu when more than one item is available, releases temporary objects, and returns 1.
Dispatches named actions for TSilverMediaListCntlr_Songs through vtable+0x114. Argument 0xdeadbeef probes action support; unrecognized actions return 0.
Reads the saved row at controller+0xd4 and retrieves its media item through the model at controller+0xb4, vtable+0x22c. Starts Genius for that item.
Builds the song context menu and stores the highlighted row at controller+0xd4. Referenced by TSilverMediaListCntlr_Songs vtable+0x148 at 0899f25c and its transition-addon vtable at 0899b4a0.

Parses root BuildIdentifier, GUID, HeapSize, Name, UserDataPath, and Version; Files DRMLevel, Digest, Path, and Size; Platforms BuildID, PlatformID, PlatformVersion, ExecutablePath, and LaunchingArtwork. Numeric text uses radix 10 through 080249a4. Files and Platforms contain dictionaries.
Dispatches named actions for TSilverMediaListCntlr_Genius through vtable+0x114. Argument 0xdeadbeef probes action support.
Reads the saved row at controller+0xd4, maps it through 08121f88, and retrieves the media item through 08121884. Starts Genius for that item.
Builds the TSilverMediaListCntlr_Genius context menu. Resolves the selected track through 08121f88 and 08121884, then saves the highlighted row at controller+0xd4.
Dispatches Settings action names such as ShowSetting_About and ShowSetting_Legal. A third argument of 0xdeadbeef suppresses execution. Menu navigation also uses serialized CEVT navigator actions.

Handles ShowSetting_About: selects GotoThreeCard_About or GotoFourCard_About from the accessory query and dispatches the UI action. Called at 0821c960. Original handler and its private literals occupy 0821cf04..0821cf8c.
Reads the volume-limit lock state, updates the lock controller state, and dispatches the ordinary volume-limit or locked-passcode screen action.
Dispatches named actions for TSilverMediaListCntlr_NestedPlaylists through vtable+0x114. Argument 0xdeadbeef probes action support.
Builds the NestedPlaylists context menu and stores the highlighted row at controller+0xe8. Referenced by TSilverMediaListCntlr_NestedPlaylists vtable+0x148 and its NestedVideoPlaylists subclass.

Submits surface+0x80 through 08114d74(surface+0x84, buffer), swaps surface+0x7c/+0x80, calls 080fb810 with the old +0x7c, then refreshes pixel pointer +0x68 from the new +0x80 through 0828c9e4(buffer,4). Called by 082c0274.

Constructs a game window surface with width/height at +0x94/+0x98. Creates two 320x240 buffer descriptors at +0x7c/+0x80 through 080fb7d0(type 2, height 240, width 320, stride 320, format 4,...). Color mode 5 gets pixel pointer +0x68 from the second descriptor through 0828c9e4(...,4), and uses 0829519c for 5:6:5 color packing.
Returns the playback-interface subobject at player+0x14, or NULL when the player singleton is unavailable.
Lazily constructs the native event-log object.
Returns the event-log singleton, allocating and constructing its 0xac-byte object on first use.
Writes queued 12-byte event records to /Logs/Data File while logging is enabled.

When enabled at +0x19, disables capture at +0x18 and drains queued 12-byte records to the binary log, appending a count record. Restores capture after success. Open failure clears the queue and resets log state.
Converts binary events to /Logs/Event Log.txt and writes a numbered summary report.

When logging is enabled, flushes the binary log, reads its 12-byte records to generate reports, and emits additional summary files. Temporarily disables capture; file errors can leave capture disabled.
Stores the enable flag at object+0x19 and prepares /Logs when enabled.
Stores the low byte of enabled at log+0x19 and prepares the logging path when enabled is nonzero. Capture state at +0x18 is managed by the flush/report routines.

Reads the manifest with a 0x20000-byte cap. If reader+4 is non-null, verifies the signature companion (cap 0x4000); a null signature path parses the unsigned manifest directly. The initial runtime read uses null; GameLoader_LoadVerifiedManifest later supplies .p7b.

Reader constructor: reader, manifestPath, storageMode, signaturePath. Stores manifestPath at +0, signaturePath at +4, storage-mode byte at +8. Null signaturePath is supported by GameManifest_ReadWithOptionalSignature.
Reads the .p7b companion and passes manifest bytes/length and signature bytes/length to 08052b30. Succeeds when the backend returns zero.
Initializes a 24-byte media item from a list entry. Stores vtable at +0 and entry pointer at +4, resolves the backing media record, and stores the third argument at +0x14.
Initializes a 24-byte media item from a song record. Stores the record at +8 and clears the list-entry pointer at +4.
Converts the four serialized VCrv edge constraints to runtime rectangle constraints, including reference IDs, offsets, and anchor kinds.
Initializes an 8-byte native string: vtable 089a6044 at +0, null data at +4. Returns the string pointer.

Seeks within the native handle under its lock; returns zero on success or a native status code. whence 0=start, 1=current (+0x34), 2=end (+0x20). Rejects positions outside [0,size]. Custom storage preserves the observed ABI: handle=r0, signed 64-bit offset low=r2/high=r3, whence=Stack[0]; r1 is padding.

Loads three biquad coefficient records for preset +0xb4 and sample rate +4. Nonzero presets at 44100/48000 Hz use banks 088feb54/088fef8c and 23-row map 088ff3c4; -1 stage index sets bypass. Each record is signed Q8.24 [b0,b1,b2,a1,a2]. Preset 0 or unsupported rate disables EQ. Expects preset already clamped to 0..22.
Clears eight 32-bit x1/x2/y1/y2 left/right history values at eq+stage*0x38+0x20..0x3c. Preserves coefficients and bypass flag. Caller supplies stage 0..2; no bounds check.
Stores preset at +0xb4, mapping unsigned values >22 to bypass 0. Reloads coefficients and calls vtable+0x10 to reset all biquad histories. Reached from property selector 2 through Audio_SetEQPreset.
Returns immediately for unchanged rate. Otherwise updates +4, reloads preset coefficients and resets histories through vtable+0x10. The loader enables nonzero presets only at 44100/48000 Hz.
Writes output_frames=input_frames. EQ vtable+0x18 sizing callback; EQ does not change frame count.
Clears histories of stages 0, 1 and 2 through EQ_ResetBiquadState. EQ vtable+0x10 reset callback; retains coefficient and bypass settings.

Processes stereo y=b0*x+b1*x1+b2*x2-a1*y1-a2*y2 with Q8.24 coefficients and signed 64-bit accumulation. Input shifts left 9; result shifts right 24 into 32-bit history, then right 9 for saturated S16 output. Independent L/R histories persist across calls. Input/output may alias. Caller supplies stage 0..2 and valid frame buffers.

Returns input pointer and frame count through output parameters. Runs stages 0..2 in place when each stage bypass byte is zero; each active stage saturates to S16 before the next. The surrounding chain checks EQ enable separately.

Installs vtable 089a61c0, sets preset 0 and disables EQ. Initializes three bypassed stages with unity b0=0x01000000, remaining coefficients zero and cleared histories. Returns eq; sample_rate +4 is initialized later.
Stores effect sample rate at +4 without recalculation or state reset. Converter vtable+0x14 uses this shared method; conversion ratio is configured separately.
Stores the low byte of enabled at effect+8. Shared converter/EQ/speed vtable+8 method; does not reset DSP state.
Appends one selection, or the whole source list for index -1, to the raw list at destination_view+4. Forwards ordering and reversal. Returns 0 for NULL source_list and 1 after dispatching an append.

TMenuView vtable+0x1cc row painter. Transforms clip/row rectangles, selects child +0xec or +0xf0, paints alternating row background when enabled, and handles selected-row styling before child draw at vtable+0x70. row_index bit 0 chooses alternating background; selected and alternate_child are zero/nonzero.
Branch thunk to MenuItem_SetVisible at 0819472c. Updates the item visibility byte and notifies resource listeners; returns 1 if the item exists, otherwise 0.

Rebuilds speed processing from input block frames +0x18 and pending float ratio +0x1207c. Sets target output frames +0x24, Q16 interpolation step +0x68, overlap lengths/weights and block period for mode 2. Unity/off disables processing and restores pass-through counts. Marks pending configuration at +0x12080; does not clear all sample buffers.

Mode 0 stores unity ratio and disables the effect. Mode 1 requests value/1000 as a floating speed ratio. Mode 2 maps -3..3 to 0.5, 2/3, 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2; other values use unity. Other modes return unchanged. A changed ratio resets overlap counters, stores pending ratio at +0x1207c and rebuilds block parameters.

Mode-2 speed processor: applies pending configuration at a block boundary, then copies/repeats/removes stereo segments and crossfades overlaps with fixed-point helpers. Uses two 0x9000-byte work areas at +0x7c/+0x907c and persistent block/carry state. Output may alias input or internal storage and frame count varies by block. Uses configured block size rather than directly reading input_frames; caller recalculates it first.

Mode-1 linear stereo interpolation. Emits configured target frames +0x24 using Q16 step +0x68, software-float interpolation and previous L/R at +0x4c/+0x4e. Updates those boundary samples. Per output frame advances input by at most two stereo frames; caller must supply a supported ratio and block size. No explicit S16 saturation is present.
