Mode 1 writes configured target frames +0x24; mode 2 writes twice that count as a capacity estimate. Other modes write input_frames. Speed-effect vtable+0x18 callback.

Recalculates layout when input frame count changes. Mode 1 interpolates into internal buffer +0x907c; mode 2 runs stereo segment/overlap processing; other modes return original pointer/count. Called as the third effect, after conversion and EQ.

Installs vtable 089a70e8, unity active/pending ratio, two channels, 1024-frame nominal blocks and four bytes per stereo frame. Sets two 0x9000-byte work buffers at +0x7c/+0x907c, clears them and resets carry/boundary sample state, then recalculates layout. Returns speed. Mode +0x44 relies on prior object storage initialization.
Returns the resource ID associated with a C++ string in the global name-to-ID map. Calls the map indexing operation, which can insert a default entry for an unknown name.
Handles bRequest 0x40. wValue 0 returns version 2; 1 returns a native status word; 2 returns paged SysInfoExtended data generated by 0x081473d0.
Setup packet at context+0x90; selects control read, zero-length write, or write-data path.
Dispatches bmRequestType 0x80/81/82, 0xa0/a1/a2, and 0xc0. Vendor-device reads use USB_HandleVendorDeviceRead.
Orders configuration interface lists {MSC} and {HID, audio control, audio streaming}; exposes one or two configurations according to the mode argument.

Requests an asynchronous game launch. Arguments: runtime, native 8-byte identifier string object, storage-mode byte, notification code. Locks +0x230 and accepts only when current state +0x22d is zero. Copies identifier to +0x24c, mode to +0x254, and event to +0x258; requests state 2. Returns 1 if accepted, 0 if busy. Caller 080f6650 passes event 0x66000003.
Destroys the game context/surface, restores saved draw/read surfaces and the prior context, then restores native display state. Called during stop state before the shutdown callback.

Creates game graphics: passes width 0x140 and height 0xf0 (320x240) to 082bffe8, obtains a context through 082bfedc, and makes it current through 082c0160. Runs on entry to active state, after init callback runtime+0x26c.
Returns the lazy singleton at 08a1b774, guarded by 089ca8b8. After acquiring the guard, calls constructor 0828bdf0, registers the destructor, and releases the guard.

Allocates a 12-byte input event: byte +0 button ID, byte +1 event type, word +4 timestamp, word +8 next pointer. Appends to runtime+0x2ac head / +0x2b0 tail. Native codes 0x6e/0x6f/0x5a/0x59/0x10 map to Menu=1, Center=2, Next=3, Previous=4, Play=5. Native types 6/0x0d map to press=2/release=1. List is exposed at frame argument+0x30 and freed after the callback.
Prepares frame state/timing and calls runtime+0x27c with r0=runtime, r1=runtime+0x100. Measures elapsed time and performs native display/update work. Corresponds to game-header callback slot 4.
Returns false for output state runtime+0x100 equal to 6 or 0. Otherwise allows one callback when runtime+0x244 equals 3, or up to 0x5b callbacks in other cases.

Converts native button messages to game events. Native types 6/0x0d become press=2/release=1. Codes 0x6e, 0x6f, 0x5a, 0x59, 0x10 become Menu=1, Center=2, Next=3, Previous=4, Play=5. Stores native message time / 1000 at event+4.
Frees the event list at runtime+0x2ac through next pointers at +8, then clears tail +0x2b0. Runs after the frame callback.
Returns platform ID from the high 16 bits of FUN_0835ed14()+0x84: 0x0b -> 1, 0x13 -> 3, 0x14 -> 2, otherwise 0.

Prepares memory/resource allocation, game storage (080a3afc), metadata (080e2c58), and audio services before executable loading. Tracks partial setup at +0x25c for cleanup. Caps the manifest-derived request at 0x1400, adds 0xc00, and passes it to 081b127c.
Sets requested-state byte +0x22c for values 0..4 and wakes waiters linked at +0x23c. Launch request uses value 2. Requested state is distinct from current-state byte +0x22d.
Returns 1 for platform-property high word 0x0b/0x13/0x14, otherwise 0. Used with GameRuntime_GetPlatformID for exact manifest platform selection.
Active-state handler: creates the graphics context, repeatedly invokes GameRuntime_InvokeFrameCallback, and dispatches input through 0828afc4. Runs in the native game task.
Invokes optional shutdown callback runtime+0x270 (game-header slot 1), computes the result state, and calls cleanup 0828b85c.

Constructs Manifest.plist path, reads it with a null signature path, prepares services, and loads the executable/resolves imports. Calls init callback runtime+0x26c, creates event/timer state, and returns to the task state machine. Loader 080f92bc performs the later signed-manifest read. Graphics creation follows in active-state handler 0828b6fc.

Loads the executable through 080f9664 and resolves imports through 080e9140. Virtual base 0x18000000 is stored at 083e2360; size cap 0x100000 at 083e235c. Reads into the translated backing address from 080858a8 and resolves using the virtual base. Stores callback count at runtime+0x268 and five callback pointers at +0x26c..+0x27c; requires +0x27c non-null.
Dispatches game task states through 16-byte records at 083e300c, indexed by runtime+0x22d. Handlers: 0828b81c idle, 0828bd54 load, 0828b6fc active, 0828b78c transition/stop.
Returns false when output state byte runtime+0x100 is 5 or 6, or internal runtime+0x244 is nonzero; otherwise true. The second frame callback argument points to runtime+0x100.
Current-state 1 handler. Calls GameRuntime_LoadManifestAndLaunch, reports the result through 080e4ae8, and synchronizes requested/current state transitions. Handler pointer is stored at 083e3020.

Constructs native game runtime and creates eAppMotor task through 080dede4, task entry 0828acf8. Initializes mutex/condition/state fields, native identifier at +0x24c, mode at +0x254. Callback outputs are stored at +0x268 (count) and +0x26c..+0x27c (five pointers).
Looks up an event name in the controller binding map at +0x94. Returns the binding payload or NULL.
Looks up event aliases in the controller map at +0x78, then the global controller map. Returns an empty list when both lookups miss.
Returns the instance count for the selected layout group, using group 1 as the fallback.
Returns the SSin record pointer at the supplied index in the selected layout group.
Returns the component-instance vector for the supplied group key. Falls back to group 1 when that key is absent.
Packs three input bytes as (b0 & 0xf8)<<8 | (b1 & 0xfc)<<3 | b2>>3. Used for surface color mode 5.
Finds the platform through 08296f7c, then matches its ExecutablePath against manifest Files entries (stride 0x20). Returns the file record used by the executable loader.
Matches both platform ID and platform version exactly in manifest platform records (stride 0x1c). Returns record or null; ID and version stored at record+4/+8.

Returns platform record +0x14 native string. Platforms[].LaunchingArtwork is relative to game directory. Stock FW2.0.4 iQuiz/Klondike/Vortex.raw.lcd5: 6176 bytes; LE32 width=55,height=55,rowBytes=112; ASCII 565L tag; 55 padded rows of little-endian RGB565 at +16.
Returns manifest file-entry byte +0x18. Parser 08208ec8 writes this for Verify (token 0x14); the game executable loader uses it to request digest/context verification. Independent of DRM byte +0x19.

Returns manifest file-entry byte +0x19. Parser 08208ec8 assigns it for the DRM key; game loader uses it to request .sinf metadata and decrypt the selected executable. This flag is separate from verification byte +0x18.

Returns the address of the inline digest descriptor at entry+0xc, not the digest bytes themselves. Game verification callers load the descriptor first word to obtain the expected-digest buffer pointer. No allocation or validation.
Accepts a media item with a list entry, or a valid song record whose database generation matches item+0x10.
Extracts the key code from bits 16 through 23 of the event word at offset +0x10.
int fn(void *handle, uint32_t *outSize). Locks handle, copies size from +0x20, returns 0 on success.
Returns the enable byte at effect+8. Shared vtable+0xc query used to gate processing and output-frame estimation.
Resolves a list entry by order and index, obtains its song record, and returns a record-backed media item. The returned item has a null list-entry pointer at +4.
Validates the playback-list wrapper, chooses its order/reversal flags, and lazily resolves the entry at zero-based index. Returns NULL when invalid, out of range, or without a usable order cache.
Checks the raw list at wrapper+4 and compares the database generation against wrapper+0xc. Returns 1 when both are valid.
Returns the current track index stored at playback_interface+0x48.

Null-safe destruction of the 16-byte scratch descriptor referenced by decryption context +4. If its first word names an allocation wrapper, clears 0x2000 bytes at wrapper+4 buffer pointer, releases that wrapper through 0839328c/0829fe4c, then clears all four descriptor words and frees the descriptor. Returns 0. The input/output page pointers used by 0835e1f4 occupy descriptor +4/+8.
Variadic debug formatter used by storage-driver diagnostics; emits through SVC 0x123456.

Formats semihosting debug output by passing format and the saved variadic argument words to Semihost_DebugVPrintf. The formatter can temporarily modify literal spans, so format storage must be writable.
Interactive RTOS console. Prints through SVC 0x123456 and reads commands with Semihost_ReadConsoleLine.

Validates backend, nonnull digest and buffered length <0x1000. Sets finalization flag 2, processes pending bytes and copies 20 digest bytes. Clears partial-block and 4 KiB workspace, releases backing and frees wrapper. Success returns zero and consumes backend ownership.
Branch thunk to GameAudio_GetService; returns the shared game-audio service pointer.
Branch thunk to GameAudio_GetService; returns the shared game-audio service pointer.
Branch thunk to GameAudio_GetService; returns the shared game-audio service pointer.

InputEvents export slot 0 (registry 08a0fda8, slot 08a0fdd4). Tail-calls 080dad8c: void(int32_t *delta, uint32_t *position_flags). Consumes accumulated wheel movement: clockwise is positive, counterclockwise negative; magnitude increases with movement speed. Position bit 30 is 1 while touching, 0 when released.
MemoryAlloc slot 1: free(void *pointer). Uses the game runtime memory manager at +0x294. Recognizes reserve blocks; otherwise releases the allocation through native heap headers.

Settings export slot 0: int(const char *name, void *out, uint32_t *inout_size). Searches three descriptors at 089ca364. HoldSwitch descriptor 089ca38c uses name 089a8be3 and callback 08088ec4: capacity >=1, writes one byte (1 locked, 0 unlocked), sets size=1, returns 0.

MemoryAlloc slot 0: void *fn(uint32_t size). Uses the manager at runtime+0x294. Rejects sizes above manager+8; near-full-block requests can use reserved blocks. On heap failure, adds unused reserve blocks through 08192090 and retries.
MemoryAlloc module slot 4 forwards to Semihost_DebugPrintf.

MemoryAlloc slot 2: void *fn(void *old, uint32_t size). Calls 081b1618 -> 081927c8 -> 08192170. Accepts NULL or pointers with native heap headers; returns 8-byte-aligned allocations. Does not replenish reserves or accept raw reserve-block pointers. Stored function extent currently covers only the prologue; the decompiler follows the continuation. Full body-boundary repair is deferred.

Gets the current surface from context getter 082c00e4. Selector 0x3059 returns context+0xae0; 0x305a returns context+0xae4. Returns zero for other selectors or no context. Surface fields: color mode byte +0x64, pixels +0x68, width +0x94, height +0x98.

OpenGLES export slot 165. Preserves r1 as the surface, calls the graphics getter and empty 08248f0c, then GameGraphics_PresentAndSwapSurface(surface). Returns 1. EGL-style two-argument wrapper; r0 display argument is unused.

Creates a 0x106c-byte aligned SHA-1 backend. Copies bytes_low&63 partial bytes, imports five chaining words with byte reversal, stores full-block byte counters and output pointer, and publishes the wrapper. Requires nonnull outputs/input/state. Returns zero or invalid-argument status; allocation failure handling is not local.
Writes the current surface pixel pointer to the output argument: 08247d14() -> +0xa8c -> +0x34 -> +0x68. The frame callback stores it at runtime+0x38. Buffer swaps change this pointer.

Opens the semihost console :tt on first use, reads up to capacity bytes through SYS_READ (6), then places NUL at buffer + capacity - unread_bytes - 2. The routine assumes a line-ending pair; short/failed reads need caller care.

Game protection wrapper: resolves storage_handle and forwards file buffer/length, manifest digest, optional data, .sinf buffer/length and context output to obfuscated backend 082e12d8 with parsed storage objects +0x60/+0x64/+0x68. Backend has 20-byte digest handling and can create a decryption context through 082de3c8. Resource callers omit .sinf/context output; executable caller checks status and nonnull context before decryption. Returns translated status. Fifth argument semantics and full backend validation remain unresolved.

Resolves the storage handle, then conditionally consumes IC-Info.rbSyncResp via record path +0xb4. Reads an allocated response, calls 082eb038 with response/record/length, frees the buffer and invokes file invalidation/removal. Follow-up paths update sidr (+0xac) and record material at +0x40. Returns status; record byte +0x8d gates processing, with exact flag meaning unresolved. Called during library FairPlay initialization.
Formats into the native scratch buffer, then emits SYS_WRITE0 (4).
Formats the variadic arguments into the shared RTXCbug scratch buffer, then emits it with semihosting SYS_WRITE0 (4). Uses shared scratch storage and requires a semihosting handler.

Null returns -50. Calls filesystem service operation 08079e80 for embedded path+4 and mode+0xc, accepting result 0 or 7 as success; other results become 0xffff5b82. File deletion is inferred from storage invalidation, consumed-response cleanup and file-replacement callers. The underlying filesystem vtable method +0x5c remains untraced.
Reads register 0x87 through 083624e0(0x87, 1, &value), writes (value & 2) >> 1 to the output pointer, and returns the read status.

Obtains an allocated vitm payload through ResolveVitmPayload. For selected ID-prefix classes removes a four-byte prefix in place and adjusts the encoded length; otherwise passes the payload through. Publishes the allocated buffer/length and returns status. Caller frees output; prefix policy remains encoded.
Adds bytes to the low counter at +0x44 and increments high counter +0x40 on unsigned carry. These count bytes; finalization converts the 64-bit count to bits.

Consumes one 64-byte block in the internal byte encoding and updates encoded chaining words. Mode 1 performs four MD5 rounds with little-endian words; mode 2 expands 80 SHA-1 words and uses four 20-round groups with big-endian input. Does not update total byte count.

Allocates replacement backing sized by the record-length delta, copies data around splice_offset and updates lengths along the root-to-record path. Publishes the new pointer/encoded size on success and wipes/frees old backing. On traversal failure restores the old descriptor and wipes/frees the replacement. Equal sizes are a no-op. Caller validates offsets and mutability.

Resets byte counters and selects mode from low byte: 1 is MD5 (16-byte output), 2 is SHA-1 (20-byte output). Initializes encoded chaining words; decoded IVs match the standard algorithms. Stores flags & 0x1ff. Unsupported modes retain zero output size and still return zero.
Tests the decoded type against 9, 150, 160, 250, 251, 260 and 380. Returns 0x93 for a match and zero otherwise. Used by verification/setup dispatch; numeric type meanings remain unresolved.

Selects one byte from each complete four-byte input word using an LCG (state = state*0xac27 + 0x9d47, index=(state&0x7f)>>5), and digests sampled bytes in groups of 64. Ignores trailing 1-3 input bytes. Re-encodes state on normal completion. Propagates full-chunk errors, but discards the final partial digest call status.

Finds root user and nested rtal records in the sidr descriptor. Builds a stack operation packet containing IDs, vitm body/length, descriptor and rtal offset; invokes 082e3254 then 0833c644, returning the mapped operation status. Does not take ownership of the body. Detailed cryptographic operations are delegated.

Computes decoded total length-offset and requires it to fit capacity; with allow_larger_capacity=0 requires exact size. Optionally returns copied length, then copies the tail using byte*0x5f-7 conversion in overlap-aware direction. Returns status. It does not separately reject offset beyond total length before unsigned subtraction.

Decodes parent/key/length argument words, finds a matching child and replaces its encoded payload through ReplaceRecordEncodedPayload. Returns argument, missing-child or replacement status. Mutability and leaf requirements are enforced by the replacement helper.

Validates the parent, walks its declared child count within the record end, and counts children whose decoded header key A matches. Returns zero for invalid parent or no matches. Does not modify the buffer.

Validates parent and searches children by decoded header key A. A positive ordinal selects that one-based match; ordinal zero retains the last matching child. Returns offset or zero and optionally publishes plain decoded key B. The match counter uses the observed 0xfffeffff mask.

Compares decoded signed limb counts, then equal-length magnitudes from the highest limb down with sign adjustment. Returns -1, 0 or 1. Expects canonical counts; unlike IsZero it does not trim redundant high zero limbs.

Resolves a vitm payload from the object descriptor or a built-in table selected by ID/platform state. Allocates and copies the selected bytes, publishes buffer/encoded length and marks the source flag. Returns lookup/allocation/copy status. Caller owns the returned allocation; built-in entries are copied rather than returned directly.
Returns 0 for numerically zero value, otherwise -1 or +1 from the decoded signed limb count. The zero test scans limbs, so a noncanonical nonzero count with all-zero limbs still returns 0.

Requires payload_bytes >=0x14 and nonnull output. Allocates payload_bytes+12 backing bytes plus a 12-byte descriptor, zeroes the prefix, stores encoded total length and flags=0. Releases backing if descriptor allocation fails. Returns zero on success or an argument/allocation status.

Creates a 0x28-byte sidd object with an empty record descriptor and initial scalar child. Stores decoded version/mode fields, copies the 24-byte identity and publishes output on success. Frees partial descriptor/object on failure. Version and mode validation use encoded arguments.

Creates a 0x24-byte sidv/sidl object with descriptor at +0x20, decoded version/mode fields and optional 24-byte identity. Creates an empty root record and publishes output only on success; cleans up on failure. Validates version/mode and output.

Finalizes the software digest, first transferring accelerated SHA-1 state back when needed. Adds encoded 0x80 padding and 64-bit bit length (MD5 little-endian, SHA-1 big-endian), writes digest_bytes in internal byte encoding, and overwrites state bytes 0..0x5f. Output must hold 16 or 20 bytes; preserves size/mode fields for outer HMAC finalization.
Copies encoded signed count and abs(decoded count) limbs, high to low. Exact self-copy is a no-op. Destination capacity is supplied by caller; no allocation or capacity check occurs.

Null-safe cleanup of storage-record +0x68 (sidb). Releases the descriptor at +0, overwrites and frees each nonnull 0x200-byte buffer at +0x28/+0x2c, then overwrites and frees the 0x34-byte object. Returns zero.

Rejects borrowed/read-only backing flags, inserts a child header and copies bytes into its payload with byte encoding x*0xa7. Copy direction follows source/destination order. Optionally returns the new offset; returns insertion/descriptor status. Source must remain valid across possible backing resize.

Null-safe cleanup of storage-record +0x6c (sidr). Releases the descriptor at +0, clears that pointer, overwrites the 0x34-byte object, and frees it. Returns zero; the apparent second return register in the old decompile is incidental.

Imports up to 256 ordinary big-endian bytes into encoded little-endian 32-bit limbs, then normalizes leading zero limbs and stores encoded count. Returns zero or length error. Input/output pointers and output capacity are caller responsibilities.

Serializes the parsed sidr object through 0x083339e0 using its backing descriptor, encoded size/flags and header at +4. Returns status; successful callers write the allocated output buffer to sidr and free it. Rejects a null object.
Scans down past zero high limbs and finds the highest set bit of the decoded magnitude. Returns 0 for zero, otherwise significant-bit count. Does not modify or normalize the stored representation.

Rejects null descriptor or an already-set decoded flag bit 0. Sets that bit, optionally publishes backing pointer and decoded length, and returns zero. The view aliases descriptor storage; this flag is a mutation/borrowing guard, not a synchronization primitive.

Computes the Montgomery product of encoded magnitudes using mont->negative_inverse, then reduces below modulus and copies into output. A zero operand produces zero. Uses fixed stack workspaces and data-dependent loops; caller must provide supported sizes and initialized Montgomery state.

Clears decoded flag bit 0 and re-encodes flags. Returns zero for nonnull descriptor, otherwise invalid-argument status. Does not free storage or invalidate an external pointer previously returned by AcquireRecordBufferView.

Converts the encoded scalar into a four-byte big-endian payload, decodes key/parent argument words and inserts it through InsertRecordEncodedPayload. ordinal is passed through; optional record_offset receives the new child. Returns argument or insertion status.

Consumes plain bytes with count-first calling convention. Software mode encodes bytes into 64-byte compression blocks and advances byte count; accelerated SHA-1 mode completes a partial software block before switching, then fills/flushes 4096-byte backend staging. Returns zero or backend error. Caller supplies a valid digest/input contract.

Returns ordinary digest bytes. Active SHA-1 backend finalizes through 0x082bba44 and clears backend pointer on success; software path finalizes to a temporary encoded digest then decodes it. Copies digest_bytes only on success. Rejects null output; returns status.

Imports encoded_input when present, otherwise plain_input; exponent NULL selects 65537. Performs modular exponentiation and exports bytes to output_e9 when supplied, otherwise output_b7, using their respective byte encodings. Writes modulus byte width multiplied by 0xc8670a7f to encoded_result_bytes. Returns zero or argument error; caller must supply a nonnull length output and valid buffers/modulus.

Builds an encoded SHA-1 digest over fixed 13-byte prefix, user/right IDs, two input spans and fixed 11-byte suffix. Transforms the middle 16 digest bytes through 08336368 and copies the resulting 20 bytes to output in its required encoding. Returns mapped transform status. Caller supplies valid spans/output; this is a format-specific derivation, not plain SHA-1.

Enumerates root vitm records from the descriptor at object+0x20 into a caller-provided 20-word array. Applies ID-prefix selection/reordering and clears unused slots. Writes count, returns argument/count/lookup status and does not allocate. The prefix policy is not fully resolved; IDs must retain their internal representation.

Walks the schi region recorded in sinf_info. Reads user/key IDs, 16-byte iviv offset, righ/name/priv offsets and lengths, and recognizes free; sets found bits in sinf_info. Enforces relevant atom sizes and exact region end. Requires flags 0x3e0 normally or 0x320 in reduced mode. Offsets refer to the supplied sinf base; caller provides fields. Returns zero or parse error.

Writes byte 0xff to persistent record 0 offset 0x14, replacing the sidr digest marker. Returns mapped storage status. This function takes no path argument despite stale caller decompiles carrying one.

Null-safe destructor for the 0x11c-byte verification object. Wipes/frees owned buffers at +0x14 and +0x100 using their encoded sizes at +0x18/+0x104, then wipes and frees the object. Does not release unrelated external pointers.

From the decoded group offset, finds head/keyB=1 then guid/keyB=1 and copies the leaf payload as plain bytes with capacity 20. Returns status and the copy helper's encoded length; requires nonnull descriptor, output and length pointers.

Exports magnitude as fixed-width big-endian bytes multiplied by 0xb7, padding leading bytes with zero. Requires output capacity at least the stored limb count times four; insufficient width silently leaves output unchanged.

Decodes input through 08303c98, checks root keys and a required scalar child, then constructs a 0x28-byte sidd object with owned descriptor, copied identity24 and decoded mode/version fields. Publishes output only on success; destroys temporary backing/object on failure. Return status is mapped through the encoded dispatcher.

Reads one ASN.1 tag/length/value from cursor. Accepts single-octet tags and definite short or 1..4-byte long lengths; rejects high-tag-number and indefinite length forms. On success advances cursor past content and returns tag, content pointer and length without copying. Bounds checks use 32-bit additions; returns zero or parse error.

Transfers SHA-1 state between encoded software storage and an aligned backend when requested mode differs from flag 0x200. Converts the partial block and five state words, moves byte counters, and updates backend pointer/flag only on successful transfer. Overwrites temporary block storage before return. Returns transfer status; callers gate further hashing on zero.

Reads the sidr file into allocated storage, computes an identity-dependent keyed digest, and compares it with the 21-byte persistent record read at record 0 offset 0. Publishes buffer and length only on success; failure paths release the temporary file buffer. Returns status. Identity is a length-prefixed byte sequence.

Finds root child vers/keyB=1 and reads its encoded 32-bit payload. Optionally writes two separately encoded fields derived from the upper/lower 16-bit portions. Returns status; NULL output pointers skip their respective writes. Output words are not plain version numbers.

For nonzero length, writes sidr then computes an identity-dependent keyed digest and stores 20 digest bytes plus a zero marker in persistent record 0. Zero length uses FairPlay_DeleteStorageFile instead. Callers do not consume a return value; internal write failures select cleanup/exit paths.

Validates request/context and encoded context flags. Uses request bytes at +0x10, preserves clear prefix/gaps/tail when copying out of place, and batches 16-byte encrypted regions through context-owned scratch buffers. Unwraps context key/IV material into temporaries and optionally updates chaining state for streaming mode. Calls 0835e1f4, whose hardware request is fixed at 4096 bytes; only selected plaintext regions are copied back. Returns status; exact flag meanings and all malformed-length behavior remain unresolved.

Reserves a new 20-byte header plus payload beneath the validated parent. key_b=0 chooses the first unused positive ID for key_a; ordinal=0 appends, otherwise inserts at the requested one-based position. Resizes/moves backing storage, writes encoded length/keys with zero child count and increments the parent child count. Writes new offset on success; returns status.
Decodes signed limb count, scans its absolute number of encoded 32-bit limbs, and returns true only when every limb is zero. Does not normalize the stored count or modify value.
Uses absolute bit_index, returns zero beyond the stored limb count, otherwise decodes the selected 32-bit limb and returns its requested bit as 0/1. Magnitude operation ignores the sign of value.

Releases the owned buffer descriptor at +0x20, overwrites the 0x24-byte object, then frees it. Used for storage-record sidv (+0x60) and sidl (+0x70) objects. Null input takes a separate status path; no owned object is freed in that case.

Squares an encoded magnitude in the Montgomery domain, reduces below modulus and writes output; zero input writes zero. Uses mont->negative_inverse and fixed stack workspaces. Caller supplies initialized state and supported operand sizes.
Tests the decoded selector against 3 through 8. Returns 0x93 for a match and zero otherwise, so this is an encoded truth result rather than a C bool. Does not modify state.

Refreshes parsed FairPlay storage state according to an obfuscated selector. Checks/loads IC-Info paths at +0xa0..0xb0 and creates/replaces parsed objects at +0x60..0x70 using identity at +0x28. Error/recovery branches release parsed objects, invalidate persisted files and reset state flags; temporary file buffers are freed. Returns status. This is mutating, allocation- and disk-I/O-capable work, not a pure handle lookup; selector meanings remain unresolved.

Selects a matching or available record in registry 089cb020, stride 0xb8, for storage-context construction. Reads stored path pointer +8 and reference count +0xc, compares path bytes through obfuscated normalization, and returns a candidate pointer or null. No allocation or reference-count write occurs here; constructor claims/initializes the returned record. Exact path normalization is unresolved.

Serializes a plain 32-bit value most-significant byte first, applies the digest byte encoding x*0x9d-0x14 and appends four bytes through DigestUpdateEncoded. Intended as a scalar-prefix helper; callers ignore the propagated register status.

Requires sidr version 0x10000, resolves user/rtal and reads rori/rwri payloads into 2048/256-byte stack buffers. Rewrites the encoded scalar at rwri+4, recalculates the trailing 20-byte rights digest at +0xec, replaces rwri and sets the dirty byte at sidr+0x21 on success. Returns lookup/copy/digest/update status.

Enumerates root grup children, reads each head/guid payload into a 20-byte stack buffer and compares against the supplied identifier. Writes the matched encoded group offset and associated keyB; returns match/argument/read status. Length and offset values use internal encodings. Does not allocate or modify records.

Creates a 32-byte encoded root record in a new descriptor. Zeroes backing, writes root length 20 at offset 12 and the two big-endian key words at offsets 16/20 using multiply-by-0xa7 byte encoding. Stores encoded total length and zero flags; publishes output on success.

Requires descriptor/data/output, validates the record and rejects nonzero decoded child count. Bounds-checks payload_offset+4 against payload length, decodes a big-endian 32-bit payload word and writes it to output. Returns zero or a descriptor/record/type/bounds status.

Feeds internally encoded bytes, buffers partial 64-byte blocks and updates byte count. Completes full blocks through DigestCompressEncodedBlock. For accelerated SHA-1, first transfers backend state to software; returns that transfer error or zero. Input bytes use the internal encoding, unlike DigestUpdatePlain.

Validates record offset and optionally returns (decoded record length-20) multiplied by 0xbd7d7cff. Output is intentionally encoded rather than a plain byte count. Returns zero on success or invalid descriptor/record status.

Finalizes inner hash into a 20-byte temporary buffer, reinitializes the same digest mode, feeds stored outer pad plus encoded inner digest, then emits ordinary output bytes. sidr callers receive a 20-byte SHA-1 HMAC. This wrapper ignores helper status values.

Validates the encoded record tree using an allocated max_depth * 12 traversal stack. Checks minimum headers, record ends, child counts, exact subtree boundaries and depth limit. Root begins at backing offset 12. Frees the stack and returns zero or argument/allocation/layout/depth error; does not modify the record tree.
Same scalar-record and four-byte bounds checks as ReadRecordU32, then multiplies decoded payload word by 0x95fcd51f before publishing it. Returns status; output is not a plain integer.

Looks up a three-key entry in a lazily allocated 512-byte cache at context+0x2c (16 entries of 32 bytes). Returns the 16-byte payload at entry+0x10 on a hit. On a miss chooses an entry using age metadata, fills it through 082f1be0, stores keys/age and advances context+0x30. Caller supplies a valid context; returns NULL on allocation/builder failure. Returned storage belongs to context and may be replaced by later lookups.

Updates value = value - subtrahend using encoded signed limb counts and encoded 32-bit magnitudes. Handles zero and opposite signs, propagates carry/borrow, flips sign if needed and removes leading zero limbs. Destination capacity is supplied by caller.

Shifts encoded integer magnitude right in place by whole limbs and remaining bits, preserving sign and normalizing encoded count. Shifting past its length writes zero. Does not clear unused trailing storage. Shared tail target of BigIntShift.

If sidr has no cached selection at +0x28, collects vitm IDs and stores two selected IDs at +0x28/+0x24. Extracts the selected vitm body, passes it with user/rights IDs to ProcessRightsRecord and frees the temporary body. Returns selection/extraction/processing status. Requires a valid sidv/sidl source.

Imports up to 256 big-endian bytes after internal digest decoding byte*0xb5-0xdc. Encodes limbs/count and normalizes high zero limbs. Returns zero or length error; the input encoding differs from ordinary bytes accepted by BigIntImportPlain.

XORs each byte with 0xc6 in place for signed positive length. Used around the obfuscated transform wrappers. Applying the same operation twice restores the input; there is no local pointer or capacity validation.

Decodes the input record backing, validates tree depth <=6, checks root keys and vers fields, and performs an optional time-related record check. On success allocates a 0x34-byte sidr object owning the descriptor, copies identity24 and initializes dirty/cache fields. Destroys temporary backing on failure. Returns an internally mapped status; detailed policy constants remain encoded.

Requires a nonzero record offset with exactly four payload bytes. Reads its big-endian scalar through ReadRecordU32 and writes an affine-encoded output, rather than a plain integer. Returns the record/argument status; output is written only after successful length and read checks.

Shifts the encoded sign/magnitude integer in place: positive bits shift left, zero/negative bits shift right by the negated amount. Preserves sign and normalizes limb count; an excessive right shift produces zero. Caller supplies capacity. Tail-branches into shared shift implementations; callers ignore the incidental register result.

Finds a child using decoded parent/key arguments, then copies its leaf payload through CopyRecordPayloadEncoded with larger capacity allowed. Reads capacity from the encoded in/out word, which is replaced by encoded payload length on success. Returns argument, missing-child or copy status.
Null-safe cleanup of storage-record +0x64 (sidd). Releases the descriptor at +0, clears that pointer, overwrites the 0x28-byte object, and frees it. Returns zero.

Null context returns 0. Otherwise calls FairPlay_DestroyDecryptionContext and returns its 32-bit status; the obfuscation multipliers reduce to identity modulo 2^32. Used in failed context creation and through game cleanup wrapper 0804bb90. Does not release a storage-registry handle.

Validates the record and optionally publishes its two header keys at +4/+8 after byte decoding plus separate affine word encodings. Returns status. The output words are encoded and must not be compared directly with plain key constants.

Initializes caller-provided one and r_squared buffers to R mod modulus and R^2 mod modulus, and stores the negative inverse of the low modulus word. R is 2^(32 * modulus limb count). Assumes a valid odd nonzero modulus; does not allocate or validate buffer capacity.

Requires mutable unborrowed backing and a leaf record. Resizes the record if needed, then replaces its payload using (x*0xb5+0x24)*0xa7 byte conversion. Returns validation/resize status; caller keeps input valid across reallocation and supplies bytes of source.

Writes an encoded sign/count and encoded magnitude limbs for the signed input. Zero sets count to zero. Caller supplies output capacity; previously stored high limbs beyond the new count remain untouched.

Decodes key/parent argument words, finds the matching child and reads its four-byte payload through ReadRecordAffineScalar. Returns an error if required pointers/keys are invalid or the child/read fails. Output remains in the scalar helper's affine encoding.

Feeds ordinary input bytes, encoding them for the software 64-byte block path. SHA-1 with flag 0x100 can switch to a backend that stages 0x1000-byte chunks. Returns zero on success or backend error; null input returns bytes and zero length returns zero. May change backend ownership and state flags.

Searches registry at 089cb020 with record stride 0xb8 for an encoded handle match. Routes the selected record through FairPlay_RefreshStorageRecord with a transformed refresh_selector; returns the record pointer or null on lookup/refresh failure. This lookup can perform disk I/O through refresh. Selector encoding and complete handle-validation rules remain unresolved.

Sets context tag at +0, clears scratch pointer +4 and allocates AES scratch there. On scratch failure destroys the whole context through FairPlay_DestroyDecryptionContext. Returns mapped allocation status; callers must not reuse context after failure.

Rejects borrowed/read-only backing flags, inserts a child and converts input bytes into record encoding with x*0x8b. Copy direction follows source/destination order. Optionally writes new record offset and returns status. Caller must keep source valid across possible backing resize.
Returns one when selector is 0, 1 or 2, otherwise zero. The two internal multipliers cancel modulo 2^32, so the external selector is plain. Pure predicate; no memory writes.

Uses the record descriptor at object+0 to find root divi/keyB=1. Reads its first big-endian payload word; a missing divi writes zero. Requires object and output, returns status, and does not create the optional record.

Validates a scalar record, decodes payload bytes with multiplier 0x17 and copies in overlap-aware direction. Requires payload length <=capacity, or exact length when allow_larger_capacity=0. Optionally publishes an encoded copied-length word. Returns status; a zero capacity permits null output only for an empty payload.

Validates a leaf record and copies its payload using x*0x1b-0x14 byte encoding. Requires payload <= capacity, or exact equality when allow_larger_capacity=0. Optional encoded_bytes receives payload size * 0xbd7d7cff. Returns zero or descriptor/record/size error; supports either copy direction.

Exports magnitude as fixed-width big-endian bytes multiplied by 0xe9, with leading zero padding. Returns without writing if output_bytes is smaller than abs(decoded limb count)*4. Ignores sign and does not return a status.

Validates an encoded record and returns its offset, or zero on failure. Offset zero means root at 12. Decodes big-endian size (minimum 20), checks end bounds/overflow and, when child count at +14 is nonzero, walks exactly that many nested records and requires their lengths to fill the parent. Internal bytes decode by multiplication by 0x17.

Tests the decoded type against 50, 51, 60, 61, 70 and 80; returns plain 0/1. Used by verification-object construction/processing. Pure predicate; the higher-level meanings of these numeric types remain unresolved.

Walks ordinary big-endian child atoms starting at sinf+8, checking minimum size and end bounds. Captures frma as a native format word, sign/schi payload offsets and sizes, and three skcr words; marks schm presence. Success requires exact end and flags frma|schm|schi (0x0b). Caller initializes info; duplicate recognized atoms overwrite prior fields.

Initializes SHA-1 mode, digests two decoded 32-bit prefixes in first-prefix then second-prefix order, then the encoded input payload and finalizes to a 20-byte encoded digest. Checks input/output pointers. Returns zero on the completed path; intermediate digest statuses are not checked.

Checks an encoded context tag, releases nonnull scratch object at +4 through 082a7398, overwrites the 0x50-byte context through an obfuscated byte loop, then frees it with 08023ef0. Returns a 32-bit status; exact tag/error encoding is unresolved. Outer release wrapper handles null. Overwrite bytes are generated values rather than a simple zero-fill.

Rejects null descriptor or null backing pointer. If bit 1 of (flags_at_8 * 3) is clear, overwrites the decoded byte count from +4 and frees backing storage at +0. Then overwrites and frees the 12-byte descriptor. Returns zero on cleanup; ownership flags and length are encoded.

Allocates an owned record buffer and converts input bytes with ((byte*0x49)-1)*0xa7. includes_prefix selects a full-buffer copy versus adding a zero 12-byte prefix. Rejects null input and short prefixed data, propagates allocation errors, and publishes the descriptor on success. Caller supplies a valid output pointer.

Walks ASN.1 elements against 28-byte encoded rules, with a fixed 16-level traversal stack. Supports optional rules, child/next indices, expected-payload comparison and callbacks receiving a 20-byte OSOS_FairPlayASN1Match. Special tag -0x1000000 accepts several ASN.1 string tags. Returns parse/callback status; callbacks may mutate their context. Does not allocate.

Allocates a 0x24-byte sidv/sidl object, decodes its backing through 08303c98, then validates the record tree with maximum depth 3. Copies the 24-byte identity and decoded mode into the object on success. On failure destroys the descriptor, wipes/frees the object and returns status.

Validates parent and walks nested records in its payload, comparing decoded header key A/B. Returns matching child offset or zero; optional ordinal is one-based. Traversal relies on the parent validation and encoded record lengths.

Computes base^exponent mod modulus for encoded integers. Converts base into Montgomery form, scans exponent bits from most to least significant with square/conditional multiply, converts out and copies to output. Uses two fixed 524-byte stack workspaces; caller initializes mont and supplies valid sizes.

Initializes HMAC with an internally encoded key. Keys longer than 64 bytes are hashed first; prepares encoded inner/outer pads using XOR 0x36/0x5c, stores outer pad at +0x68 and feeds the 64-byte inner pad. Null or zero-length key returns without initializing state. sidr callers use a 24-byte encoded key and mode 2 (SHA-1).

Shifts encoded integer magnitude left in place by whole limbs and remaining bits, preserving sign, filling low limbs with zero and updating encoded count. Caller supplies enough capacity. Shared tail target of BigIntShift; argument order is bits then value.

Validates the user-ID argument and requires sidr version at +0x2c to equal 0x10000, then dispatches to ApplySidrRightsFromSidv with decoded/re-encoded scalar arguments. Returns mapped argument/version/processing status. Caller provides a valid sidr pointer.
Waits on RTOS signal 0x38, blocks tasks, and enters RTXCbug_MainMenu.

Calls locked hardware AES using input=scratch+4 pointer, output=scratch+8 pointer, supplied key/IV, selector 0 and a fixed length of 0x1000 bytes. Returns 0 on hardware status 0, otherwise 0xffff5b32. Caller 0831bf88 also places a byte count on the stack, but this wrapper never reads it; both scratch buffers must hold a full page.

Copies bytes sequentially to state+0 when both pointers are nonnull; returns zero after copying or 9 for a null pointer. Used by SHA feed for 0..63 trailing bytes. No local length/capacity check; caller must supply a nonnegative count fitting the partial block.

Early startup dependency, reached via file 0x422C -> veneer 0x3DE8 -> runtime 0x0835ED5C (this file offset). Calls file 0x2BD84C with r0=0x18; helper returns 0x2203FF00+r0. Requires word at 0x2203FF18 == 0x53797349; mismatch returns 0x52. Reads source pointer from 0x2203FF1C, copies 0x120 bytes to runtime 0x08A11CD8. Startup later reads this structure's +0xE0 size and +0xE4 base to establish DRAM mappings. Strong evidence of boot-stage handoff data; producer and complete descriptor format not established from this image.

Queries the prior resource-gate state for mask (0,1), enables that resource and clears control at MMIO 0x3c100000. Returns the previous gate-state token for RestoreHardware. Does not itself read a random word or acquire a mutex.
Restores the (0,1) resource-gate setting using the token from PrepareHardware. Tail-calls the platform gate service; does not clear software initialization state.
Polls MMIO 0x3c100000 until status bits 0..2 are nonzero, then returns the word at +4. Assumes hardware has been prepared. Has no timeout, error return or allocation.
Return site after startup call 08081e60. Task creation and startup run earlier through 0805d558.
Formats %d, %u, %x/%X, %s and %c; emits SYS_WRITEC (3) and SYS_WRITE0 (4).

Walks the format string and ARM variadic argument words, emitting text through semihosting. Supports decimal, unsigned, hex, character, string and percent conversions with limited width handling. Literal spans are temporarily NUL-terminated by Semihost_WriteSpan, so format must be writable.

Null returns -50; an already-set byte 0 returns 0. Otherwise checks embedded path+4 using storage mode +0xc: an existing path returns 0xffff5b81; an absent path sets byte 0 and returns 0xffff5b80. This is a state/status query, not a simple exists boolean.

Checks buffered length <0x1000 and internal digest pointer, processes pending data without final padding, then exports the 64-byte partial block, counters and five byte-reversed chaining words. Clears workspace, releases backing and frees wrapper on success. Returns status; caller must clear its backend reference.

Allocates bytes+0x40, rounds the usable pointer up to 32-byte alignment and stores raw/aligned pointers separately. When address bit 27 is set, invokes the cache helper and uses an alias with bit 31 set. Sets initialized only after allocation success and returns storage; the visible byte-count loop writes no data.

Clears initialized and releases nonnull allocation through allocator kind 3. Returns the wrapper without freeing it or clearing either stored pointer. Caller must free the wrapper separately and avoid a second release of the stale allocation pointer.
English SettingsMenu_About_String, ID 0x0dad0b44: About followed by NUL and padding. OSOS file offset 0x802614. Resource record at 0x41bdd0 is {ID, 0x3df614, 6}; resource base is 0x423000.

Game Audio module, version 1, 54 exports. Function table +0x2c; next module 08a103b8 (Metadata). Wrappers 082bbb94..082bbffc use GameAudio_GetService for media playback controls, settings, timing, and track properties. Constructor 0817f138 stores MediaPlayer_GetInstance at service+0 and command dispatcher 080f5c9c at +4.

Confirmed startup copy path; addresses in this raw import are FILE OFFSETS. Let P be the runtime address of file offset 0x800; incoming r0 = 0x22000000 - P. Copies P -> 0x22000000, length 0xAED8; clears 0x2200AED8..0x22010774 (exclusive); adjusts LR by relocation delta at file 0x90E8 and continues in IRAM. Copies P+0xAED8 -> 0x08000000 length 0xA0FC88, then P+0xA1AB60 -> 0x08A0FC88 length 0xA84. Finally BX 0x22000000 restarts relocated vector. Copy helper 0x8D4 handles overlapping ranges. Runtime mapping: IRAM = file-0x800+0x22000000; main DRAM = file-0xB6D8+0x08000000. These are fixed section copies, not pointer fixups. Direct plaintext boot has not been tested.

Runs at IRAM 220071b0. r0=output queue, r1=position. Stores position at +0x13c and all 32 slots +0x34..+0xb0. Common reset reached from queue rebuild 220072cc, metadata clear 22007294, and underrun recovery 22007260. Called around decoder repositioning in 220054a8 via those reset paths. Synthesized-audio history must be invalidated when these queue positions reset.
